at tabe.explanation: "At tabe" means "to lose", as in a contest. To say you lose a game, say: "Vi taber kampen" (We lose the match). To say you let something fall, it also means "to drop": "Jeg tabte min telefon" (I dropped my phone). To say you cannot find an item, use "at miste" (to lose something) instead: "Jeg har mistet min nøgle" (I have lost my key).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **tabe** glasset på gulvet.
sentence.en: I don't want to drop the glass on the floor.

at tabe sig.explanation: "At tabe sig" means "to lose weight". Literally, it is "to lose oneself". Without "sig" (oneself), "at tabe" means "to drop". For example, "Jeg tabte min telefon" (I dropped my phone).

sentence.da: Han vil **tabe sig** og spiser mere grønt.
sentence.en: He wants to lose weight and eats more vegetables.

at tage.explanation: "At tage" means "to take". To say you go by a vehicle, use it with the vehicle: "tage bussen" (take the bus). To say you are going somewhere, it also means "to go": "Jeg tager til København" (I am going to Copenhagen).

sentence.da: Du kan **tage** en kage fra bordet.
sentence.en: You can take a cake from the table.

at tage af.explanation: "At tage af" means "to take off", as in clothes. To say you remove your jacket, say: "Jeg tager jakken af" (I take my jacket off). To tell a guest to take their coat off, say: "Kom ind og tag af!" (Come in and take your coat off!)

related.en: to put on, to gain weight

sentence.da: Jeg har det varmt og vil **tage af**.
sentence.en: I feel warm and want to take something off.

at tage af bordet.explanation: "At tage af bordet" means "to clear the table". Literally, it is "to take off the table". To ask someone for help after a meal, say: "Kan du tage af bordet?" (Can you clear the table?)

sentence.da: Efter maden skal vi **tage af bordet**.
sentence.en: After the meal we have to clear the table.

at tage af sted.explanation: "At tage af sted" means "to set off". To name the place you set off for, add "til" (to): "Vi tager af sted til Aarhus" (We set off for Aarhus).

sentence.da: Vi skal **tage af sted** om ti minutter.
sentence.en: We have to set off in ten minutes.

at tage bad.explanation: "At tage bad" means "to take a shower". To say you soak in the tub, use "at tage et karbad" (to take a bath in the tub): "Jeg tager et karbad om aftenen" (I take a bath in the evening).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage bad** efter løbeturen.
sentence.en: I want to take a shower after the run.

at tage bussen.explanation: "At tage bussen" means "to take the bus". For other transport, use "tage" (take) too: "Jeg tager toget til København" (I take the train to Copenhagen).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage bussen** til arbejde.
sentence.en: I want to take the bus to work.

at tage det roligt.explanation: "At tage det roligt" means "to take it easy". To tell someone to calm down, say it as a command: "Tag det roligt!" (Calm down!)

sentence.da: I weekenden vil jeg **tage det roligt** hjemme.
sentence.en: On the weekend I want to take it easy at home.

at tage en beslutning.explanation: "At tage en beslutning" means "to make a decision". Danish uses "tage" (take) here where English uses "make". To say a decision will come soon, say: "Vi tager en beslutning i morgen" (We will make a decision tomorrow).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **tage en beslutning** inden fredag.
sentence.en: I have to make a decision before Friday.

at tage en uddannelse.explanation: "At tage en uddannelse" means "to get an education". Danish uses "tage" (take) here. To ask what someone is training for, say: "Hvilken uddannelse tager du?" (Which education are you taking?)

sentence.da: Efter gymnasiet vil han **tage en uddannelse** som elektriker.
sentence.en: After high school, he wants to train as an electrician.

at tage et billede.explanation: "At tage et billede" means "to take a picture". To say it another way, use "at tage et foto" (to take a photo). To suggest a picture of the group, say: "Skal vi tage et billede sammen?" (Shall we take a picture together?)

sentence.da: Må jeg **tage et billede** af dig?
sentence.en: May I take a picture of you?

at tage fat.explanation: "At tage fat" means "to get to work or grab hold". To say you grab something physically, add "i" (in): "tage fat i rebet" (grab hold of the rope). To say you start a task, add "på" (on): "tage fat på arbejdet" (get to work on it).

forms.en: to get to work / grab hold
I get to work / grab hold
I got to work / grabbed hold
I have gotten to work / grabbed hold

sentence.da: Vi skal **tage fat** på renoveringen i morgen.
sentence.en: We have to get started on the renovation tomorrow.

at tage fejl.explanation: "At tage fejl" means "to be wrong", about an opinion or a guess. For example, "Du tager fejl" (You are wrong). To say you made a mistake in a task, use "en fejl" (a mistake): "Jeg lavede en fejl" (I made a mistake).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt **tage fejl**, men det tror jeg ikke.
sentence.en: I could be wrong, but I do not think so.

at tage fri.explanation: "At tage fri" means "to take time off", when you decide it yourself. For example, "Jeg tager fri i morgen" (I am taking tomorrow off). When you are allowed to leave, use "at få fri" (to get off): "Jeg fik fri klokken tre" (I got off at three).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage fri** på mandag.
sentence.en: I want to take Monday off.

at tage hensyn.explanation: "At tage hensyn" means "to be considerate". It is built from "tage" (take) and "et hensyn" (a consideration). To name the person you consider, add "til" (to): "Du skal tage hensyn til de andre" (You have to be considerate of the others).

sentence.da: Man skal **tage hensyn** til naboerne.
sentence.en: You have to be considerate of the neighbors.

at tage hensyn til.explanation: "At tage hensyn til" means "to take into account". To say what you take into account, put it after "til" (to): "Jeg tager hensyn til dit helbred" (I take your health into account).

sentence.da: Vi skal **tage hensyn til** naboerne om natten.
sentence.en: We must be considerate of the neighbors at night.

at tage hjem.explanation: "At tage hjem" means "to go home". Here "tage", which normally means "take", means "go". For example, "Jeg tager hjem klokken fem" (I go home at five o'clock).

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **tage hjem** efter arbejde.
sentence.en: We would like to go home after work.

at tage imod.explanation: "At tage imod" means "to receive or accept". To say you accept something offered, say: "Hun tog imod hjælpen" (She accepted the help). To say you welcome people who arrive, say: "Vi tager imod gæsterne klokken fem" (We receive the guests at five o'clock).

sentence.da: Han vil ikke **tage imod** penge fra os.
sentence.en: He will not accept money from us.

at tage med.explanation: "At tage med" means "to bring along or come along". To say you bring something, say: "Jeg tager en jakke med" (I bring a jacket along). To ask to join someone, say: "Må jeg tage med?" (May I come along?)

forms.en: I have brought along / come along

sentence.da: Vil du **tage med** os i biografen?
sentence.en: Do you want to come along with us to the movies?

at tage medicin.explanation: "At tage medicin" means "to take medicine". To ask whether someone has done it, say: "Har du taget din medicin?" (Have you taken your medicine?)

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og skal **tage medicin**.
sentence.en: I am sick and have to take medicine.

at tage noter.explanation: "At tage noter" means "to take notes". To say where you take them, add "i timen" (in class): "Jeg tager noter i timen" (I take notes in class).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage noter**, fordi jeg glemmer alt.
sentence.en: I want to take notes because I forget everything.

at tage op.explanation: "At tage op" means "to pick up or take up". To say you lift something from the floor, say: "Jeg tager bogen op fra gulvet" (I pick the book up from the floor). To say you start a new hobby, say: "Hun tog golf op" (She took up golf).

forms.en: I have picked up / taken up

sentence.da: Det vil jeg gerne **tage op** på mødet.
sentence.en: I would like to take that up at the meeting.

at tage på.explanation: "At tage på" means "to gain weight". For example, "Jeg har taget på i vinter" (I have gained weight this winter). To say you go on a trip, use it with "ferie" (vacation): "Vi tager på ferie" (We are going on vacation).

sentence.da: Hvis du spiser meget kage, kan du **tage på**.
sentence.en: If you eat a lot of cake, you can gain weight.

at tage på ferie.explanation: "At tage på ferie" means "to go on vacation". It is built from "at tage på" (to go on a trip) and "ferie" (vacation). To say you are already on vacation, use "at være på ferie" (to be on vacation): "Jeg er på ferie i denne uge" (I am on vacation this week).

sentence.da: Vi vil **tage på ferie** til Spanien.
sentence.en: We want to go to Spain on vacation.

at tage sig af.explanation: "At tage sig af" means "to take care of". To say you look after a person, say: "Hun tager sig af sin syge mor" (She takes care of her sick mother). To say you handle a chore, say: "Jeg tager mig af opvasken" (I take care of the dishes).

sentence.da: Han vil **tage sig af** hunden i weekenden.
sentence.en: He will take care of the dog on the weekend.

at tage sig sammen.explanation: "At tage sig sammen" means "to pull oneself together". To tell someone to make an effort, say: "Nu må du tage dig sammen!" (Now you must pull yourself together!)

related.da: at tage sig selv i nakken

sentence.da: Hun vil gerne **tage sig sammen** og begynde at træne.
sentence.en: She wants to pull herself together and start working out.

at tage sig tid.explanation: "At tage sig tid" means "to take one's time". To tell someone not to rush, say: "Tag dig tid!" (Take your time!) To name what you take time for, add "til at" (to) before the verb: "Han tager sig tid til at tænke" (He takes his time to think).

sentence.da: Man kan **tage sig tid**, når der ikke er travlt.
sentence.en: You can take your time when there is no rush.

at tage skeen i den anden hånd.explanation: "At tage skeen i den anden hånd" means "to change your approach". Literally, it is "to take the spoon in the other hand". To say you will change your approach after a failure, say: "Nu tager jeg skeen i den anden hånd" (Now I will change my approach).

forms.da: Han tog skeen i den anden hånd
Vi må tage skeen i den anden hånd
Nu tager hun skeen i den anden hånd
forms.en: Now she is changing her approach

sentence.da: Vi bruger for mange penge og må **tage skeen i den anden hånd**.
sentence.en: We spend too much money and must change our approach.

at tage skraldet ud.explanation: "At tage skraldet ud" means "to take out the trash". The word "ud" (out) comes after "skraldet" (the trash). To tell someone to do it, say: "Tag skraldet ud!" (Take out the trash!)

forms.en: I have taken out the trash

sentence.da: Kan du **tage skraldet ud**, når du går?
sentence.en: Can you take out the trash when you leave?

at tage stilling til.explanation: "At tage stilling til" means "to take a position on". To say you have not decided yet, say: "Jeg har ikke taget stilling endnu" (I have not made up my mind yet). To name the matter you decide on, put it after "til" (on): "at tage stilling til forslaget" (to take a position on the proposal).

forms.en: I have taken a position on

sentence.da: Du skal **tage stilling til** tilbuddet i dag.
sentence.en: You have to take a position on the offer today.

at tage tid.explanation: "At tage tid" means "to take time". To say something takes time, start with "det" (it): "Det tager tid at lære dansk" (It takes time to learn Danish). To say it takes a long time, add "lang" (long): "Det tager lang tid" (It takes a long time).

sentence.da: Det vil **tage tid** at bygge et hus.
sentence.en: It will take time to build a house.

at tage toget.explanation: "At tage toget" means "to take the train". The past form of "at tage" (to take) is "tog", which is spelled like "et tog" (a train). In "Jeg tog toget" (I took the train), the first "tog" is the verb and "toget" is the noun.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage toget** til København.
sentence.en: I want to take the train to Copenhagen.

at tage tyren ved hornene.explanation: "At tage tyren ved hornene" means "to take the bull by the horns". To say you are about to deal with a problem right now, say: "Nu tager jeg tyren ved hornene og ringer til banken" (Now I will take the bull by the horns and call the bank).

forms.en: She takes the bull by the horns

forms.da: Nu må vi tage tyren ved hornene
forms.en: Now we must take the bull by the horns
He took the bull by the horns

sentence.da: Hun besluttede at **tage tyren ved hornene** og tale med chefen.
sentence.en: She decided to take the bull by the horns and talk to the boss.

at tage ud.explanation: "At tage ud" means "to go out or take out". To say you leave home to go somewhere, say: "Vi tager ud til stranden" (We go out to the beach). To say you remove something from inside, say: "Jeg tager skraldet ud" (I take the trash out).

sentence.da: Vi vil **tage ud** og spise i aften.
sentence.en: We want to go out and eat tonight.

at takke.explanation: "At takke" means "to thank". To say what you thank someone for, add "for" (for): "Jeg takker dig for maden" (I thank you for the food).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **takke** dig for hjælpen.
sentence.en: I would like to thank you for the help.

at tale.explanation: "At tale" means "to speak". To say you speak to a group, say: "Han taler til holdet" (He speaks to the team). To name the person, add "med" (with): "Jeg taler med min chef" (I speak with my boss). To name the topic, add "om" (about): "Vi taler om planen" (We speak about the plan).

sentence.da: Kan du **tale** dansk?
sentence.en: Can you speak Danish?

at tale med.explanation: "At tale med" means "to talk to". To ask for a person on the phone, say: "Kan jeg tale med Anna?" (Can I speak to Anna?)

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **tale med** dig.
sentence.en: I would like to talk to you.

at tale med store bogstaver.explanation: "At tale med store bogstaver" means "to speak bluntly". Literally it is "to speak with huge print", meaning you say it loudly and clearly: "Han talte med store bogstaver til mig" (He spoke bluntly to me).

forms.da: Nu taler vi med store bogstaver
Jeg må tale med store bogstaver

sentence.da: Når han ikke forstår hints, må jeg **tale med store bogstaver**.
sentence.en: When he does not get hints, I have to speak bluntly.

at tale om.explanation: "At tale om" means "to talk about" a topic. In a question, "om" (about) stays at the end. For example, "Hvad taler I om?" (What are you talking about?)

sentence.da: Vi vil **tale om** vejret i dag.
sentence.en: We want to talk about the weather today.

at tale sammen.explanation: "At tale sammen" means "to talk (with each other)". The word "sammen" (together) shows that the people talk to each other. For example, "Vi taler sammen hver dag" (We talk to each other every day). To name the other person, use "at tale med" (to talk with): "Jeg taler med min mor" (I talk with my mother).

sentence.da: Vi skal **tale sammen** om det i morgen.
sentence.en: We need to talk about it tomorrow.

at tale sandt.explanation: "At tale sandt" means "to tell the truth". The word "sandt" (true) is a form of "sand" (true). For the same meaning, you can say "at sige sandheden" (to tell the truth): "Jeg vil sige sandheden" (I want to tell the truth).

sentence.da: Jeg vil altid **tale sandt**, også når det er svært.
sentence.en: I will always tell the truth, even when it is hard.

at tale ud.explanation: "At tale ud" means "to talk things through". The word "ud" (out) adds the idea of finishing completely. For example, "Lad mig tale ud!" (Let me finish speaking!) Do not mix it up with "at tale udenom" (to beat around the bush). To tell someone to get to the point, say: "Tal ikke udenom!" (Do not beat around the bush!)

sentence.da: Efter skænderiet ville parret **tale ud** med hinanden.
sentence.en: After the argument, the couple wanted to talk it out with each other.

at tale udenom.explanation: "At tale udenom" means "to beat around the bush". "Udenom" means "around the outside", so the picture is circling the topic and never reaching it. To tell someone to get to the point, say: "Tal ikke udenom!" (Do not beat around the bush!) Do not mix it up with "at tale ud" (to talk things through). To say you want to settle things, say: "Lad os tale ud" (Let us talk things through).

forms.en: You are beating around the bush

forms.da: Hold op med at tale udenom

forms.en: He beat around the bush the whole time

sentence.da: Hun bliver ved med at **tale udenom**, når jeg spørger om pengene.
sentence.en: She keeps beating around the bush when I ask about the money.

at tanke.explanation: "At tanke" means "to refuel". To say you put fuel in your car, say: "Jeg tanker bilen" (I fill up the car). To say you charge an electric car, use "at lade" (to charge): "Jeg lader bilen" (I charge the car).

sentence.da: Bilen er næsten tom, og jeg skal **tanke**.
sentence.en: The car is almost empty, and I have to refuel.

at taste.explanation: "At taste" means "to type or enter". To say you key in a number, say: "Jeg taster telefonnummeret" (I enter the phone number). To say you write a letter, use "at skrive" (to write): "Jeg skriver et brev" (I write a letter).

sentence.da: Du skal **taste** din pinkode og trykke OK.
sentence.en: You have to enter your PIN and press OK.

at tegne.explanation: "At tegne" means "to draw". To say what someone draws, name it after the verb: "Han tegner en hund" (He draws a dog). To say you paint with paint, use "at male" (to paint): "Hun maler et billede" (She paints a picture).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tegne** et hus med en blyant.
sentence.en: I want to draw a house with a pencil.

at teste.explanation: "At teste" means "to test". To say you try out something new, say: "Vi tester den nye app" (We are testing the new app). To say you have a test at school, use the noun "en prøve" (a test or exam): "Vi har en prøve i morgen" (We have a test tomorrow).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **teste** os i matematik i morgen.
sentence.en: The teacher will test us in math tomorrow.

at tigge.explanation: "At tigge" means "to beg". To say what you beg for, add "om" (for): "Børnene tigger om slik" (The children beg for candy).

sentence.da: Han måtte **tigge** om mad, fordi han ingenting havde.
sentence.en: He had to beg for food because he had nothing.

at tilbagebetale.explanation: "At tilbagebetale" means "to pay back". It is built from "tilbage" (back) and "at betale" (to pay). To say a shop returns money, say: "Butikken tilbagebetaler beløbet" (The store pays the amount back). To say you pay a person back, use "at betale tilbage" (to pay back): "Jeg betaler dig tilbage i morgen" (I will pay you back tomorrow).

sentence.da: Du skal **tilbagebetale** hele lånet inden for fem år.
sentence.en: You must pay back the whole loan within five years.

at tilbagekalde.explanation: "At tilbagekalde" means "to recall or revoke". It is built from "tilbage" (back) and "at kalde" (to call). To say a company takes a faulty product back, say: "Firmaet tilbagekalder produktet" (The company recalls the product).

sentence.da: Firmaet måtte **tilbagekalde** bilerne, fordi bremserne ikke virkede.
sentence.en: The company had to recall the cars because the brakes did not work.

at tilbagevise.explanation: "At tilbagevise" means "to refute". It is built from "tilbage" (back) and "at vise" (to show). To say someone answers an accusation by proving it false, say: "Han tilbageviste beskyldningen" (He refuted the accusation).

sentence.da: Hun vil **tilbagevise** beskyldningen, fordi den ikke er sand.
sentence.en: She will refute the accusation because it is not true.

at tilbede.explanation: "At tilbede" means "to worship". To say you love a person almost without limit, use it for the person: "Fansene tilbeder hende" (The fans adore her).

sentence.da: I kirken kan man **tilbede** Gud sammen med andre.
sentence.en: In church, people can worship God together.

at tilberede.explanation: "At tilberede" means "to prepare (food)". To say you cook a meal, say: "Jeg tilbereder aftensmaden" (I prepare dinner). To say you get ready for something else, use "at forberede" (to get ready): "Jeg forbereder mig til eksamen" (I am preparing for the exam).

sentence.da: Kokken vil **tilberede** fisken i ovnen og servere den.
sentence.en: The chef will prepare the fish in the oven and serve it.

at tilbringe.explanation: "At tilbringe" means "to spend (time)". It is only used for time: "Vi tilbringer sommeren i Skagen" (We spend the summer in Skagen). To say you spend money, use "at bruge" (to spend): "Jeg bruger 100 kroner" (I spend 100 kroner).

sentence.da: Vi vil **tilbringe** sommeren i Jylland.
sentence.en: We want to spend the summer in Jutland.

at tilbyde.explanation: "At tilbyde" means "to offer". To say you offer someone something, name the person first, then the thing: "Jeg tilbyder dig kaffe" (I offer you coffee).

sentence.da: Må jeg **tilbyde** dig en kop te?
sentence.en: May I offer you a cup of tea?

at tildele.explanation: "At tildele" means "to assign or award". To say a boss gives someone a task, say: "Chefen tildeler mig opgaven" (The boss assigns me the task). To say someone receives a prize, say: "Hun blev tildelt prisen" (She was awarded the prize).

sentence.da: Skolen vil **tildele** prisen til den bedste elev.
sentence.en: The school will award the prize to the best student.

at tilføje.explanation: "At tilføje" means "to add". To say you want to say one more thing, say: "Jeg vil tilføje en ting" (I want to add one thing). To add numbers together, use "at lægge sammen" (to add up): "Jeg lægger tallene sammen" (I add up the numbers).

sentence.da: Du kan **tilføje** lidt salt til suppen.
sentence.en: You can add a little salt to the soup.

at tilgive.explanation: "At tilgive" means "to forgive". To say what you forgive a person, name the person first, then the thing: "Hun tilgav ham alt" (She forgave him everything).

sentence.da: Hun vil **tilgive** ham, når han siger undskyld.
sentence.en: She will forgive him when he says sorry.

at tilhøre.explanation: "At tilhøre" means "to belong to". Unlike English, you add no word for "to" after it: "Huset tilhører staten" (The house belongs to the state).

sentence.da: En bog kan **tilhøre** biblioteket eller en privat person.
sentence.en: A book can belong to the library or to a private person.

at tilintetgøre.explanation: "At tilintetgøre" means "to annihilate". It is built from "til intet" (to nothing) and "at gøre" (to make), so literally it is "to make into nothing". To say a storm wipes out a harvest, say: "Stormen tilintetgjorde høsten" (The storm wiped out the harvest).

sentence.da: Branden kunne **tilintetgøre** hele skoven på en nat.
sentence.en: The fire could annihilate the whole forest in one night.

at tilkalde.explanation: "At tilkalde" means "to summon or call in". It is built from "til" (to) and "at kalde" (to call). To say you call a professional to come to you, say: "Vi tilkalder lægen" (We call in the doctor).

sentence.da: Hvis det brænder, skal du **tilkalde** brandvæsenet med det samme.
sentence.en: If there is a fire, you must call in the fire department right away.

at tillade.explanation: "At tillade" means "to allow". To say what you yourself may do, use "at have lov til" (to be allowed to): "Jeg har lov til at gå" (I am allowed to go).

sentence.da: Reglerne vil ikke **tillade** hunde i butikken.
sentence.en: The rules will not allow dogs in the store.

at tilmelde sig.explanation: "At tilmelde sig" means "to sign up". The word "sig" (oneself) changes with who signs up. To say she signs up, use "sig": "Hun tilmelder sig" (She signs up). To say we sign up, use "os": "Vi tilmelder os" (We sign up).

sentence.da: Alle skal **tilmelde sig** inden fredag.
sentence.en: Everyone has to sign up before Friday.

at tilpasse.explanation: "At tilpasse" means "to adapt". To say you change a recipe so it suits you, say: "Jeg tilpasser opskriften" (I adapt the recipe). To say you change yourself, add "sig" (oneself): "at tilpasse sig" (to adapt yourself).

sentence.da: Vi skal **tilpasse** planen, så den passer til alle.
sentence.en: We must adapt the plan so it suits everyone.

at tilpasse sig.explanation: "At tilpasse sig" means "to adapt". The word "sig" (oneself) turns the action back on the person doing it. To say a person adapts quickly, say: "Hun tilpasser sig hurtigt" (She adapts quickly).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **tilpasse sig**, når man flytter til et nyt land.
sentence.en: It is hard to adapt when you move to a new country.

at tilsidesætte.explanation: "At tilsidesætte" means "to disregard or override". It is built from "til side" (to the side) and "at sætte" (to put). To say someone ignores a rule, say: "Chefen tilsidesatte reglerne" (The boss disregarded the rules).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke bare **tilsidesætte** reglerne, fordi du har travlt.
sentence.en: You cannot just disregard the rules because you are busy.

at tilskynde.explanation: "At tilskynde" means "to encourage". To name what you want people to do, add "til at" (to) before the verb: "Prisen tilskynder folk til at spare energi" (The price encourages people to save energy).

sentence.da: Lærerne vil **tilskynde** eleverne til at læse mere.
sentence.en: The teachers want to encourage the students to read more.

at tilstræbe.explanation: "At tilstræbe" means "to strive for". Unlike English, you add no word for "for" after it. To say what you strive for, name it right after the verb: "Vi tilstræber fred" (We strive for peace).

sentence.da: Firmaet vil **tilstræbe** en bedre kvalitet i år.
sentence.en: The company will strive for better quality this year.

at tilstå.explanation: "At tilstå" means "to confess". To say someone confesses without naming anything, use the verb alone: "Han tilstod" (He confessed). To name the crime, put it directly after the verb: "Han tilstod tyveriet" (He confessed to the theft).

sentence.da: Tyven vil **tilstå**, fordi politiet har fundet billederne.
sentence.en: The thief will confess because the police have found the pictures.

at tiltrække.explanation: "At tiltrække" means "to attract". To say a shop draws people, say: "Butikken tiltrækker mange kunder" (The store attracts many customers). To say a magnet pulls iron, say: "Magneten tiltrækker jern" (The magnet attracts iron).

sentence.da: Den nye park kan **tiltrække** mange turister om sommeren.
sentence.en: The new park can attract many tourists in the summer.

at tisse.explanation: "At tisse" means "to pee". It is an informal word. To say you need to go, say: "Jeg skal tisse" (I need to pee). To say it politely, say: "Jeg skal på toilettet" (I need to go to the toilet).

sentence.da: Barnet skal **tisse** på toilettet.
sentence.en: The child has to pee in the toilet.

at tjekke.explanation: "At tjekke" means "to check". To say you look at something to see that it is right, say: "Jeg tjekker mine mails" (I am checking my email). To say a doctor looks into a problem, use "at undersøge" (to examine): "Lægen undersøger mig" (The doctor examines me).

sentence.da: Han vil **tjekke** dækkene før turen.
sentence.en: He wants to check the tires before the trip.

at tjene.explanation: "At tjene" means "to earn or serve". To say you get paid for work, say: "Jeg tjener 300 kroner i timen" (I earn 300 kroner an hour). To say something is useful for a purpose, say: "Det tjener et formål" (It serves a purpose).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **tjene** flere penge.
sentence.en: I would like to earn more money.

at tjene penge.explanation: "At tjene penge" means "to earn money". To say you spend money, use "at bruge penge" (to spend money): "Jeg bruger penge på mad" (I spend money on food).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tjene penge** i sommerferien.
sentence.en: I want to earn money during the summer vacation.

at tolerere.explanation: "At tolerere" means "to tolerate". To say you will not put up with something, say: "Jeg tolererer ikke støj om natten" (I do not tolerate noise at night). To say your body cannot take something, use "at tåle" (to stand): "Jeg tåler ikke mælk" (I cannot handle milk).

sentence.da: Man skal **tolerere** andres meninger, også når man er uenig.
sentence.en: You must tolerate other people's opinions, even when you disagree.

at tordne.explanation: "At tordne" means "to thunder". To say it is thundering, start with "det" (it): "Det tordner" (It is thundering). The noun is "en torden" (thunder), and a storm with thunder is "et tordenvejr" (a thunderstorm).

sentence.da: Det begynder at **tordne**, og himlen bliver helt mørk.
sentence.en: It starts to thunder, and the sky gets completely dark.

at trampe.explanation: "At trampe" means "to stomp". To say people crush something under their feet, add "på" (on): "Børnene trampede på blomsterne" (The children trampled the flowers).

sentence.da: Den vrede dreng begynder at **trampe** i gulvet.
sentence.en: The angry boy starts to stomp on the floor.

at transportere.explanation: "At transportere" means "to transport". To say a company carries goods by vehicle, say: "Firmaet transporterer varer med lastbil" (The company transports goods by truck). To say you take a person home by car, use "at køre" (to drive): "Jeg kører dig hjem" (I will drive you home).

sentence.da: Lastbilen skal **transportere** frugt fra Spanien til Danmark.
sentence.en: The truck must transport fruit from Spain to Denmark.

at trives.explanation: "At trives" means "to thrive". To say you feel at home in a place, say: "Jeg trives i Aarhus" (I feel at home in Aarhus). To say a plant does well, say: "Planten trives i skygge" (The plant thrives in shade).

sentence.da: Han kan **trives** i en lille by, fordi alle kender hinanden.
sentence.en: He can thrive in a small town because everyone knows each other.

at tro.explanation: "At tro" means "to believe". To say you think something is probably true, say: "Jeg tror, det er rigtigt" (I think it is right). To say you have faith, add "på" (in): "at tro på Gud" (to believe in God). To give your own taste, use "at synes" (to think): "Jeg synes, det er godt" (I think it is good).

related.en: to think / to be of the opinion

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **tro** det!
sentence.en: I can't believe it!

at tro på.explanation: "At tro på" means "to believe in". To say you believe in a person, say: "Jeg tror på dig" (I believe in you). To say you merely think something, leave out "på" (in): "Jeg tror, det regner" (I think it is raining).

sentence.da: Børn vil gerne **tro på** julemanden.
sentence.en: Children like to believe in Santa Claus.

at trodse.explanation: "At trodse" means "to defy". To say a child does not obey, say: "Barnet trodser sine forældre" (The child defies his parents). To say a thing does not give way to a force, say: "Huset trodsede stormen" (The house defied the storm).

sentence.da: Hun vil **trodse** forbuddet og tage derhen alligevel.
sentence.en: She will defy the ban and go there anyway.

at true.explanation: "At true" means "to threaten". To name what someone threatens to do, use "med" (with): "Han truer med at sige op" (He threatens to quit). To say bad weather is coming, start with "det" (it): "Det truer med regn" (Rain is threatening).

sentence.da: Naboen kan **true** med at ringe til politiet.
sentence.en: The neighbor can threaten to call the police.

at trykke.explanation: "At trykke" means "to press or print". To say you press a button, say: "Jeg trykker på knappen" (I press the button). To say you print books or posters, say: "Vi trykker bogen" (We print the book).

sentence.da: Du skal **trykke** på den grønne knap.
sentence.en: You have to press the green button.

at træde.explanation: "At træde" means "to step". To say you step into a place, add "ind" (in): "Han trådte ind i huset" (He stepped into the house). To say you step out, add "ud" (out): "Hun trådte ud på gaden" (She stepped out into the street).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **træde** på blomsterne.
sentence.en: You must not step on the flowers.

at træde i kraft.explanation: "At træde i kraft" means "to take effect". Literally, it is "to step into force". To say a rule starts tomorrow, say: "Reglen træder i kraft i morgen" (The rule takes effect tomorrow).

sentence.da: Loven skal **træde i kraft** den første januar.
sentence.en: The law must take effect on the first of January.

at træde tilbage.explanation: "At træde tilbage" means "to step down or resign". To say a leader gives up the post, say: "Formanden trådte tilbage" (The chair stepped down). To say you quit an ordinary job, use "at sige op" (to quit): "Jeg siger op" (I quit).

sentence.da: Ministeren vil **træde tilbage**, fordi hun har mistet støtten.
sentence.en: The minister will step down because she has lost support.

at træffe.explanation: "At træffe" means "to meet or make (a decision)". To say you run into someone, say: "Jeg traf Anna i byen" (I ran into Anna in town). To say you make an agreement, say: "at træffe en aftale" (to make an agreement).

sentence.da: Du kan **træffe** mig på kontoret efter klokken tre.
sentence.en: You can reach me at the office after three o'clock.

at træffe en beslutning.explanation: "At træffe en beslutning" means "to make a decision". It is built from "at træffe" (to make) and "en beslutning" (a decision). To say the same with "tage" (to take), say: "Jeg tager en beslutning i dag" (I take a decision today).

sentence.da: Når vi er uenige, skal chefen **træffe en beslutning**.
sentence.en: When we disagree, the boss must make a decision.

at trække.explanation: "At trække" means "to pull". To say you pull a suitcase behind you, say: "Jeg trækker kufferten" (I pull the suitcase). To say you breathe, use the phrase "trække vejret" (to breathe): "Han trækker vejret dybt" (He breathes deeply).

sentence.da: Vi må **trække** i rebet sammen.
sentence.en: We have to pull on the rope together.

at trække fra.explanation: "At trække fra" means "to subtract". To say you take one number away from another, say: "Jeg trækker tre fra ti" (I subtract three from ten). To say you deduct an amount, say: "Man kan trække det fra i skat" (You can deduct it on your taxes).

sentence.da: Du skal **trække fra** og ikke lægge sammen.
sentence.en: You have to subtract and not add.

at trække på skuldrene.explanation: "At trække på skuldrene" means "to shrug". It is built word for word from "at trække" (to pull), "på" (on) and "skuldrene" (the shoulders). To say someone shrugged when asked, say: "Han trak på skuldrene" (He shrugged).

sentence.da: Når jeg spørger hvorfor, plejer hun at **trække på skuldrene**.
sentence.en: When I ask why, she usually shrugs.

at trække sig.explanation: "At trække sig" means "to withdraw". The word "sig" (oneself) shows that you pull yourself out. To name what you withdraw from, add "fra" (from): "Hun trak sig fra valget" (She withdrew from the election).

sentence.da: Han vil **trække sig** fra aftalen, fordi prisen er for høj.
sentence.en: He wants to withdraw from the deal because the price is too high.

at trække vejret.explanation: "At trække vejret" means "to breathe". Literally, it is "to pull the breath", with "vejret" meaning "the breath". The same word "vejret" also means "the weather". To say the weather is nice, say: "Vejret er flot i dag" (The weather is nice today).

sentence.da: Du skal **trække vejret** dybt.
sentence.en: You must breathe deeply.

at træne.explanation: "At træne" means "to train". To say you practice a skill, name it after the verb: "Jeg træner dansk hver dag" (I practice Danish every day).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **træne** tre gange om ugen.
sentence.en: I want to work out three times a week.

at trænge.explanation: "At trænge" means "to need or push through". To say something forces its way in, say: "Vandet trænger ind" (The water gets in). To say you really need something, add "til" (for): "Jeg trænger til ferie" (I really need a vacation).

sentence.da: Lyset kan **trænge** ind gennem de tynde gardiner.
sentence.en: The light can get in through the thin curtains.

at trøste.explanation: "At trøste" means "to comfort". To say how you comfort someone, add "med" (with): "Hun trøster ham med et kram" (She comforts him with a hug).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **trøste** min ven, fordi han har mistet sit job.
sentence.en: I want to comfort my friend because he has lost his job.

at tude.explanation: "At tude" means "to cry or howl". To tell a child to stop crying loudly, say: "Hold op med at tude!" (Stop bawling!) To say a siren makes a long loud sound, say: "Sirenen tuder" (The siren is wailing). It is an informal word.

sentence.da: Barnet begyndte at **tude**, da ballonen sprang.
sentence.en: The child started to bawl when the balloon popped.

at tvinge.explanation: "At tvinge" means "to force". To name the action the person is forced to perform, add "til at" (to) before the verb: "Hun tvang ham til at spise" (She forced him to eat).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke **tvinge** mig til at komme.
sentence.en: You cannot force me to come.

at tvivle.explanation: "At tvivle" means "to doubt". To say what you doubt, add "på" (on): "Jeg tvivler på, at han kommer" (I doubt that he is coming).

sentence.da: Hun begynder at **tvivle** på sig selv.
sentence.en: She is starting to doubt herself.

at tvivle på.explanation: "At tvivle på" means "to doubt". To say you doubt that something will happen, start the second part with "at" (that): "Jeg tvivler på, at han kommer" (I doubt that he is coming). To say you are unsure, use "at være i tvivl" (to be in doubt): "Jeg er i tvivl" (I am unsure).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke **tvivle på** mig.
sentence.en: Do not doubt me.

at tyde.explanation: "At tyde" means "to interpret". To ask someone to read old handwriting, say: "Kan du tyde det gamle brev?" (Can you interpret the old letter?) Do not mix it up with "at tyde på" (to suggest / indicate). To say the signs point to something, say: "Det tyder på regn" (It suggests rain).

sentence.da: Jeg kan næsten ikke **tyde** hans håndskrift.
sentence.en: I can hardly interpret his handwriting.

at tyde på.explanation: "At tyde på" means "to suggest or indicate". To say the signs lead to a conclusion, say: "Alt tyder på, at det bliver koldt" (Everything suggests that it will be cold). Do not mix it up with "at tyde" (to interpret), which has no "på" (on). To say you read hard writing, say: "Jeg tyder skriften" (I interpret the writing).

sentence.da: Alle de mørke skyer kan **tyde på** regn.
sentence.en: All the dark clouds can suggest rain.

at tygge.explanation: "At tygge" means "to chew". To name what you chew on, add "på" (on): "Hunden tygger på en pind" (The dog chews on a stick). The word "tyggegummi" (chewing gum) is built from "at tygge" (to chew) and "gummi" (rubber).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **tygge**, fordi min tand gør ondt.
sentence.en: I cannot chew because my tooth hurts.

at tåle.explanation: "At tåle" means "to tolerate or stand". To say you cannot stand something, use it with "ikke" (not): "Jeg tåler ikke larm" (I cannot stand noise). To say a material can take something, say: "Tøjet tåler vask" (The clothes can take washing).

sentence.da: Min mave kan ikke **tåle** stærk mad.
sentence.en: My stomach cannot handle spicy food.

at tælle.explanation: "At tælle" means "to count". Its past forms "jeg talte" (I counted) and "jeg har talt" (I have counted) are the same as the past forms of "at tale" (to speak). To say you counted, say: "Jeg talte pengene" (I counted the money). To say you spoke, say: "Vi talte hele natten" (We talked all night).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **tælle** til ti.
sentence.en: I can count to ten.

at tænde.explanation: "At tænde" means "to turn on". To say you light a candle or a fire, use it too: "Vi tænder bålet" (We light the fire). To say you turn on a TV, a radio or running water, add "for" (for): "Jeg tænder for radioen" (I turn on the radio).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tænde** lyset i mørket.
sentence.en: I want to turn on the light in the dark.

at tænde for.explanation: "At tænde for" means "to turn on". To say you turn on a radio, a TV or the water, add "for" (for): "Jeg tænder for radioen" (I turn on the radio). To say you turn on a light, use "at tænde" (to turn on, to light): "Jeg tænder lyset" (I turn on the light).

sentence.da: Jeg fryser og vil **tænde for** varmen.
sentence.en: I am cold and want to turn on the heating.

at tænke.explanation: "At tænke" means "to think". To say someone is on your mind, add "på" (of): "Jeg tænker på dig" (I am thinking of you). To give an opinion, use "at synes" (to think, to have an opinion): "Jeg synes, det er godt" (I think it is good).

sentence.da: Lad mig **tænke** lidt.
sentence.en: Let me think a little.

at tænke over.explanation: "At tænke over" means "to think about". To say you are thinking a matter over, say: "Jeg tænker over det" (I am thinking it over). To say someone is on your mind, use "at tænke på" (to think of): "Jeg tænker på dig" (I am thinking of you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **tænke over** dit tilbud.
sentence.en: I would like to think about your offer.

at tænke på.explanation: "At tænke på" means "to think of". To say a person is on your mind, say: "Jeg tænker på min mor" (I am thinking of my mother). To say you are thinking a matter over, use "at tænke over" (to think about): "Jeg tænker over det" (I am thinking it over).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke holde op med at **tænke på** ferien.
sentence.en: I cannot stop thinking about the vacation.

at tænke sig om.explanation: "At tænke sig om" means "to think carefully". The word "sig" (oneself) changes with who is thinking. For example, "jeg tænker mig om" (I think carefully), "han tænker sig om" (he thinks carefully).

sentence.da: Man bør **tænke sig om**, før man svarer.
sentence.en: You should think carefully before you answer.

at tø.explanation: "At tø" means "to thaw". To say it is thawing, start with "det" (it): "Det tør" (It is thawing). The same spelling "tør" is also the word for "dry". For example, "tør hud" (dry skin). It is also the word for "dare". For another example, "Jeg tør ikke" (I do not dare).

sentence.da: Når det begynder at **tø**, bliver sneen til vand.
sentence.en: When it starts to thaw, the snow turns to water.

at tømme.explanation: "At tømme" means "to empty". The adjective "tom" (empty) is the related word, so "at tømme" makes something "tom". To say you empty a bin, say: "Jeg tømmer skraldespanden" (I empty the trash can).

sentence.da: Kan du **tømme** opvaskemaskinen for mig?
sentence.en: Can you empty the dishwasher for me?

at tørre.explanation: "At tørre" means "to dry". To say something loses its water, say: "Tøjet tørrer hurtigt" (The clothes dry quickly). To say you wipe a surface, add "af" (off): "Jeg tørrer bordet af" (I wipe the table off).

sentence.da: Håndklæderne skal **tørre** i solen.
sentence.en: The towels have to dry in the sun.

at tørre af.explanation: "At tørre af" means "to wipe or dry (dishes)". To say you wipe a table, say: "Han tørrer bordet af" (He wipes the table). To say you dry plates, say: "Hun tørrer tallerkenerne af" (She dries the plates). To mop up a spill, use "at tørre op" (to wipe up): "Jeg tørrer vandet op" (I wipe up the water).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **tørre af** efter middagen.
sentence.en: I have to dry the dishes after dinner.

at tørre støv af.explanation: "At tørre støv af" means "to dust". It is built from "at tørre" (to wipe), "støv" (dust) and "af" (off). To say how often someone dusts, put "af" (off) at the end: "Han tørrer støv af hver uge" (He dusts every week).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **tørre støv af** på hylderne i dag.
sentence.en: I have to dust the shelves today.

en t-shirt.explanation: "En t-shirt" means "a t-shirt". To say you wear one, use "at have" (to have) with "på" (on): "Jeg har en t-shirt på" (I am wearing a t-shirt). Literally, it is "I have a t-shirt on".

sentence.da: Om sommeren går jeg i **t-shirt** og shorts.
sentence.en: In the summer I wear a t-shirt and shorts.

en tabel.explanation: "En tabel" means "a table", as in rows and columns of information. To say the piece of furniture, use "et bord" (a table): "Bogen ligger på bordet" (The book is on the table).

sentence.da: Tallene står i en **tabel** på side tre.
sentence.en: The numbers are in a table on page three.

en tablet.explanation: "En tablet" means "a tablet", as in the flat touchscreen computer. To say a pill, use the same word: "Jeg tager en tablet mod smerter" (I take a pill for pain).

sentence.da: Jeg læser nyheder på min **tablet** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I read the news on my tablet every morning.

en tagrende.explanation: "En tagrende" means "a gutter". It is built from "tag" (roof) and "rende" (channel). To say rainwater runs into it, use "ned i": "Regnvandet løber ned i tagrenden" (The rainwater runs down into the gutter).

sentence.da: Regnvand løber ned i en **tagrende**.
sentence.en: Rainwater runs down into a gutter.

en tagterrasse.explanation: "En tagterrasse" means "a roof terrace". To say where you sit or eat, use "på": "Vi spiser på tagterrassen" (We eat on the roof terrace).

sentence.da: Fra vores **tagterrasse** kan vi se hele byen.
sentence.en: From our roof terrace we can see the whole city.

en taktik.explanation: "En taktik" means "a tactic". To say a team has a way of playing, use it with the team: "Holdets taktik er at forsvare sig" (The team's tactic is to defend). "En strategi" (a strategy) is the plan for a long time ahead. For example, "Vi har en strategi for de næste fem år" (We have a strategy for the next five years).

sentence.da: Holdets **taktik** er at forsvare sig og vente på en chance.
sentence.en: The team's tactic is to defend and wait for a chance.

en talemåde.explanation: "En talemåde" means "a saying". It is built from "tale" (speech) and "måde" (way). A saying whose words do not mean what they say is "at tage benene på nakken" (to run away fast, literally "to take the legs on the neck").

sentence.da: Man skal ikke tage hver **talemåde** helt bogstaveligt.
sentence.en: You should not take every saying completely literally.

en tallerken.explanation: "En tallerken" means "a plate". To ask for the kind of plate that holds soup, say "en dyb tallerken" (a deep plate): "Jeg vil gerne have suppe på en dyb tallerken" (I would like soup on a deep plate).

sentence.da: Der er mad på min **tallerken**.
sentence.en: There is food on my plate.

en talsperson.explanation: "En talsperson" means "a spokesperson". To say a man speaks for a group, use "en talsmand" (a spokesman): "Han er foreningens talsmand" (He is the association's spokesman).

sentence.da: Virksomhedens **talsperson** svarede på journalisternes spørgsmål i går.
sentence.en: The company's spokesperson answered the journalists' questions yesterday.

en tand.explanation: "En tand" means "a tooth". To say you brush your teeth, use the plural: "Jeg børster tænder" (I brush my teeth). Many words start with it, such as "en tandbørste" (a toothbrush).

sentence.da: Jeg har ondt i en **tand** i dag.
sentence.en: One of my teeth hurts today.

en tandbøjle.explanation: "En tandbøjle" means "a dental brace". It is built from "tand" (tooth) and "bøjle" (hoop). To say someone wears braces, leave out "en": "Hun har tandbøjle" (She wears braces).

sentence.da: Min datter skal have **tandbøjle**, fordi hendes tænder står skævt.
sentence.en: My daughter needs braces because her teeth are crooked.

en tandbørste.explanation: "En tandbørste" means "a toothbrush". It is built from "tand" (tooth) and "børste" (brush). To say you brush your teeth, use "at børste tænder" (to brush teeth): "Jeg børster tænder to gange om dagen" (I brush my teeth twice a day).

sentence.da: Jeg børster tænder med en **tandbørste**.
sentence.en: I brush my teeth with a toothbrush.

en tandlæge.explanation: "En tandlæge" means "a dentist". It is built from "en tand" (a tooth) and "en læge" (a doctor). To say you have a dentist visit, use "skal til" (am going to): "Jeg skal til tandlægen" (I am going to the dentist).

sentence.da: Min **tandlæge** kigger på mine tænder.
sentence.en: My dentist looks at my teeth.

en tandlægetid.explanation: "En tandlægetid" means "a dentist appointment". It is built from "tandlæge" (dentist) and "tid" (time or appointment). To say you have no time, use "tid" for time: "Jeg har ikke tid" (I have no time). To say you have an appointment, use "tid" for appointment: "Jeg har en tid klokken ti" (I have an appointment at ten).

sentence.da: Til min **tandlægetid** kigger tandlægen på mine tænder.
sentence.en: At my dentist appointment, the dentist looks at my teeth.

en tandplejer.explanation: "En tandplejer" means "a dental hygienist". It is built from "tandpleje" (dental care).

sentence.da: Min **tandplejer** renser mine tænder to gange om året.
sentence.en: My dental hygienist cleans my teeth twice a year.

en tang.explanation: "En tang" means "a pair of pliers or seaweed". When you talk about the tool for gripping or cutting wire, use "en tang": "Jeg klipper ledningen over med en tang" (I cut the wire in two with pliers). When you talk about seaweed on the beach, leave out "en": "Der ligger tang på stranden" (There is seaweed on the beach).

sentence.da: Jeg kan klippe ledningen over med en **tang**.
sentence.en: I can cut the wire in two with pliers.

en tank.explanation: "En tank" means "a tank". To say what a tank holds, put a word in front: "en vandtank" (a water tank). To say you put fuel in a car, use "på": "Vi fylder benzin på bilens tank" (We put gas in the car's tank).

sentence.da: Vi fylder benzin på bilens **tank**.
sentence.en: We put gas in the car's tank.

en tanke.explanation: "En tanke" means "a thought". To thank someone for a kind idea, say "Tak for tanken" (Thanks for the thought). To say you have thought about something, use the plural: "Jeg har gjort mig tanker om det" (I have thought about it).

sentence.da: Jeg havde en **tanke**: Vi kan tage toget.
sentence.en: I had a thought: We can take the train.

en tankstation.explanation: "En tankstation" means "a gas station". It is built from "at tanke" (to fill up) and "en station" (a station). To say you need to fill up the car, use the verb alone: "Jeg skal lige tanke" (I just need to fill up the car).

sentence.da: Tanken er tom, og vi leder efter en **tankstation**.
sentence.en: The tank is empty, and we are looking for a gas station.

en tante.explanation: "En tante" means "an aunt". To say an aunt is your mother's sister, use "en moster": "Min moster bor i Aarhus" (My mother's sister lives in Aarhus). To say an aunt is your father's sister, use "en faster": "Min faster bor i Odense" (My father's sister lives in Odense).

sentence.da: Min **tante** er min mors søster.
sentence.en: My aunt is my mother's sister.

en tarm.explanation: "En tarm" means "an intestine". To name the parts, put "tyk" (thick) or "tynd" (thin) in front: "en tyktarm" (a large intestine) and "en tyndtarm" (a small intestine).

sentence.da: En voksens **tarm** er flere meter lang og ligger i maven.
sentence.en: An adult's intestine is several meters long and lies in the belly.

en tartelet.explanation: "En tartelet" means "a tartlet (vol-au-vent)". In Denmark, the classic filling is chicken and asparagus in sauce. For example, "tarteletter med høns i asparges" (tartlets with chicken in asparagus).

sentence.da: Hun fyldte hver **tartelet** med høns og asparges.
sentence.en: She filled each tartlet with chicken and asparagus.

en taske.explanation: "En taske" means "a bag, purse". To name the kind of bag, put a word in front: "en håndtaske" (a handbag) and "en skoletaske" (a school bag). To ask for a plastic shop bag, use "en pose" (a plastic bag): "Må jeg få en pose?" (May I have a bag?)

sentence.da: Jeg har bøger i min **taske**.
sentence.en: I have books in my bag.

en tatovering.explanation: "En tatovering" means "a tattoo". It comes from the verb "at tatovere" (to tattoo). To say you will get one, use "få" (get): "Jeg vil have en tatovering" (I want a tattoo).

sentence.da: Hun har en **tatovering** af en rose på armen.
sentence.en: She has a tattoo of a rose on her arm.

en tavle.explanation: "En tavle" means "a blackboard". To name another kind of board, put a word in front: "en opslagstavle" (a bulletin board). To say something hangs there: "Der hænger en seddel på opslagstavlen" (A note hangs on the bulletin board).

sentence.da: Der hænger en stor **tavle** i klasseværelset.
sentence.en: A big blackboard hangs in the classroom.

en tavshed.explanation: "En tavshed" means "a silence". To say someone ended the silence, use "at bryde" (to break): "Han brød tavsheden" (He broke the silence). For quiet with no sound around you, use "stilhed" (quiet): "Der er stilhed i skoven" (It is quiet in the forest).

sentence.da: Der var en lang **tavshed**, fordi ingen turde sige noget.
sentence.en: There was a long silence because nobody dared to say anything.

en taxa.explanation: "En taxa" means "a taxi". To say how you travel, use "med" (by) without an article: "Vi kører med taxa" (We go by taxi). To say you book one, use "at bestille" (to book): "Jeg bestiller en taxa" (I am booking a taxi).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **taxa** til lufthavnen.
sentence.en: We take a taxi to the airport.

en taxachauffør.explanation: "En taxachauffør" means "a taxi driver". It is built from "en taxa" (a taxi) and "en chauffør" (a driver). To tell the driver where you want to go, say "Til banegården, tak" (To the railway station, please).

sentence.da: En **taxachauffør** kører folk rundt i byen.
sentence.en: A taxi driver drives people around the city.

en teenager.explanation: "En teenager" means "a teenager". The word comes from English. To say what someone is, leave out "en": "Hun er teenager" (She is a teenager).

sentence.da: Min søn er **teenager** og sover længe.
sentence.en: My son is a teenager and sleeps late.

en tegnebog.explanation: "En tegnebog" means "a wallet". The word "en pung" also means "a wallet". For example, "Har du din pung?" (Do you have your wallet?)

sentence.da: Jeg har penge og kort i min **tegnebog**.
sentence.en: I have money and cards in my wallet.

en tegnefilm.explanation: "En tegnefilm" means "a cartoon". It is built from "at tegne" (to draw) and "en film" (a film). The kind you read is "en tegneserie" (a comic). For example, "Jeg læser en tegneserie" (I am reading a comic).

sentence.da: I en **tegnefilm** er alle figurerne tegnet.
sentence.en: In a cartoon, all the characters are drawn.

en tegner.explanation: "En tegner" means "an illustrator". It comes from the verb "at tegne" (to draw). What an illustrator makes is "en tegning" (a drawing). For example, "Tegneren afleverer en tegning i dag" (The illustrator hands in a drawing today).

sentence.da: En **tegner** laver billederne til bogen, og forfatteren skriver teksten.
sentence.en: An illustrator makes the pictures for the book and the author writes the text.

en tegneserie.explanation: "En tegneserie" means "a comic". It is built from "at tegne" (to draw) and "en serie" (a series). The kind you watch is "en tegnefilm" (a cartoon). For example, "Børnene ser en tegnefilm" (The children are watching a cartoon).

sentence.da: En **tegneserie** har billeder og små talebobler.
sentence.en: A comic has pictures and small speech bubbles.

en tegning.explanation: "En tegning" means "a drawing". It comes from the verb "at tegne" (to draw). To say someone draws, use the verb: "Barnet tegner et hus" (The child draws a house).

sentence.da: Man laver en **tegning** med en blyant.
sentence.en: You make a drawing with a pencil.

en tekande.explanation: "En tekande" means "a teapot". It is built from "te" (tea) and "kande" (pot). To say you pour tea, use "hælde op" (to pour): "Jeg hælder te op" (I pour tea).

sentence.da: Jeg brygger te i en **tekande**.
sentence.en: I brew tea in a teapot.

en teknologi.explanation: "En teknologi" means "a technology". To talk about the field in general, leave out "en": "Han er interesseret i teknologi" (He is interested in technology).

sentence.da: Ny **teknologi** gør livet nemmere for mange.
sentence.en: New technology makes life easier for many.

en tekst.explanation: "En tekst" means "a text". To talk about the words of a song, use the same word: "Jeg kender teksten til sangen" (I know the lyrics of the song). To talk about subtitles on a film, put "under" (under) in front: "Filmen har danske undertekster" (The film has Danish subtitles).

sentence.da: En **tekst** kan være en artikel eller en besked.
sentence.en: A text can be an article or a message.

en tekstforfatter.explanation: "En tekstforfatter" means "a lyricist or copywriter". When you talk about someone who writes the words for songs, it means "a lyricist": "Han er tekstforfatter for flere sangere" (He is a lyricist for several singers). When you talk about someone who writes ads, it means "a copywriter": "Han er tekstforfatter på et reklamebureau" (He is a copywriter at an advertising agency).

sentence.da: Hun er **tekstforfatter** og skriver ord til andres melodier.
sentence.en: She is a lyricist and writes words for other people's melodies.

en telefon.explanation: "En telefon" means "a phone". To say mobile phone, use "en mobil": "Jeg har glemt min mobil" (I forgot my mobile phone). To call someone, use "at ringe til" (to call): "Jeg ringer til dig" (I will call you).

sentence.da: Med en **telefon** kan jeg ringe hjem.
sentence.en: With a phone I can call home.

en temperatur.explanation: "En temperatur" means "a temperature". To say someone has a fever, use "at have feber" (to have a fever): "Jeg har feber" (I have a fever). To ask how warm it is, say "Hvad er temperaturen?" (What is the temperature?)

sentence.da: Tyve grader er en god **temperatur**.
sentence.en: Twenty degrees is a good temperature.

en tendens.explanation: "En tendens" means "a trend". To say what something tends to do, add "til" (toward): "en tendens til stress" (a tendency toward stress).

sentence.da: Der er en **tendens** til, at priserne stiger hvert år.
sentence.en: There is a tendency for prices to rise every year.

en teori.explanation: "En teori" means "a theory". To say something works on paper but not in real life, use "praksis" (practice): "I teorien virker det, men i praksis gør det ikke" (In theory it works, but in practice it does not).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **teori**, men jeg kan ikke bevise den.
sentence.en: I have a theory, but I can't prove it.

en tepose.explanation: "En tepose" means "a tea bag". It is built from "te" (tea) and "pose" (bag). To name other bags, put a word in front of "pose": "en indkøbspose" (a shopping bag).

sentence.da: Jeg putter en **tepose** i det varme vand.
sentence.en: I put a tea bag in the hot water.

en terapeut.explanation: "En terapeut" means "a therapist". To name the kind, put a word in front: "en fysioterapeut" (a physical therapist). To say you have a visit, use "skal til" (am going to): "Jeg skal til fysioterapeuten" (I am going to the physical therapist).

sentence.da: Min **terapeut** hjælper mig med at tale om mine bekymringer.
sentence.en: My therapist helps me talk about my worries.

en termin.explanation: "En termin" means "a due date". When you talk about a baby, it is the day the baby is expected: "Barnets termin er i maj" (The baby's due date is in May). When you talk about a loan, it is the day a payment is due: "Terminen på lånet er den første" (The loan payment is due on the first).

sentence.da: Næste **termin** på lånet skal betales den første i måneden.
sentence.en: The next installment on the loan must be paid on the first of the month.

en termokande.explanation: "En termokande" means "a thermos". It is built from "termo" (heat) and "kande" (jug). To say what is in it, put the drink right after: "en termokande kaffe" (a thermos of coffee).

sentence.da: Vi har kaffe i en **termokande** på turen.
sentence.en: We have coffee in a thermos on the trip.

en termokop.explanation: "En termokop" means "a travel mug". It is built from "termo" (heat) and "en kop" (a cup). To say what you bring in it: "Jeg tager kaffe med i min termokop" (I take coffee along in my travel mug).

sentence.da: Min **termokop** holder kaffen varm i flere timer.
sentence.en: My travel mug keeps the coffee warm for several hours.

en terning.explanation: "En terning" means "a die or cube". To say you roll dice in a game, use "at slå med" (to roll): "Jeg slår med terningen" (I roll the die). To say a cube of food, put a word in front: "en bouillonterning" (a bouillon cube).

sentence.da: Du skal slå med en **terning**, og så flytter du brikken.
sentence.en: You roll a die, and then you move the piece.

en terrasse.explanation: "En terrasse" means "a terrace". To say where you sit outside, use "på" (on): "Vi sidder på terrassen" (We sit on the terrace).

sentence.da: Huset har en **terrasse** med havemøbler.
sentence.en: The house has a terrace with garden furniture.

en terrorist.explanation: "En terrorist" means "a terrorist". The word for what a terrorist does is "terrorisme" (terrorism). For example, "Politiet bekæmper terrorisme" (The police fight terrorism).

sentence.da: En **terrorist** bruger vold og gør folk bange.
sentence.en: A terrorist uses violence and scares people.

en teske.explanation: "En teske" means "a teaspoon". It is built from "te" (tea) and "ske" (spoon). To give an amount in a recipe, put the food right after: "en teske sukker" (a teaspoon of sugar).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **teske** sukker i min kaffe.
sentence.en: I take a teaspoon of sugar in my coffee.

en tid.explanation: "En tid" means "a time". To say how many times something happens, use "en gang" (one time): "Jeg har været der to gange" (I have been there twice). To say an hour, use "en time" (an hour): "Det tager en time" (It takes an hour).

sentence.da: Det tager lang **tid** at lære dansk.
sentence.en: It takes a long time to learn Danish.

en tid hos lægen.explanation: "En tid hos lægen" means "a doctor's appointment" (literally, "a time at the doctor"). To say a dentist appointment, change the end: "en tid hos tandlægen" (an appointment at the dentist).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **tid hos lægen** i dag.
sentence.en: I have a doctor's appointment today.

en tidsel.explanation: "En tidsel" means "a thistle". To say you remove weeds from a garden, use "at luge" (to weed): "Jeg luger tidsler i haven" (I am weeding thistles in the garden).

sentence.da: En **tidsel** har skarpe pigge og en lilla blomst.
sentence.en: A thistle has sharp spikes and a purple flower.

en tidsfrist.explanation: "En tidsfrist" means "a time limit". To say you meet it, use "at overholde" (to keep to): "Vi overholder tidsfristen" (We meet the time limit). To say you go past it, use "at overskride" (to exceed): "Han overskrider tidsfristen" (He goes past the time limit).

sentence.da: Vi arbejder hurtigt, fordi vi har en **tidsfrist** på fredag.
sentence.en: We work fast because we have a deadline on Friday.

en tidsplan.explanation: "En tidsplan" means "a schedule". It is built from "tid" (time) and "plan" (plan). To say you keep to it, use "at holde" (to keep): "Vi holder tidsplanen" (We keep to the schedule).

sentence.da: Vi har en stram **tidsplan** i denne uge.
sentence.en: We have a tight schedule this week.

en tidszone.explanation: "En tidszone" means "a time zone". It is built from "tid" (time) and "en zone" (a zone).

sentence.da: Sverige er i samme **tidszone** som Danmark.
sentence.en: Sweden is in the same time zone as Denmark.

en tiger.explanation: "En tiger" means "a tiger". The "g" is not pronounced, so the word sounds like "TEE-uh". To talk about a young tiger, add "unge" (young animal): "en tigerunge" (a tiger cub).

sentence.da: En **tiger** er en stor kat med striber.
sentence.en: A tiger is a big cat with stripes.

en tigger.explanation: "En tigger" means "a beggar". To say someone begs for money, use the verb "at tigge" (to beg): "Han tigger penge" (He begs for money).

sentence.da: En **tigger** sidder på gaden med en kop til mønter.
sentence.en: A beggar sits on the street with a cup for coins.

en tilbagebetaling.explanation: "En tilbagebetaling" means "a refund or repayment". When you talk about money a shop gives back, it means "a refund": "Jeg fik en tilbagebetaling for den ødelagte vare" (I got a refund for the broken item). When you talk about paying back a loan, it means "a repayment": "Tilbagebetalingen af lånet starter i januar" (The repayment of the loan starts in January).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **tilbagebetaling** for den ødelagte vare.
sentence.en: I got a refund for the broken item.

en tilbagegang.explanation: "En tilbagegang" means "a decline". To say something is shrinking, use "i tilbagegang" (in decline): "Salget er i tilbagegang" (Sales are declining). The opposite is "en fremgang" (progress). For example, "Der er fremgang i salget" (Sales are improving).

sentence.da: Butikken har haft en **tilbagegang** i salget i flere måneder.
sentence.en: The store has had a decline in sales for several months.

en tilbagemelding.explanation: "En tilbagemelding" means "feedback". To say you will answer later, use it like this: "Jeg giver dig en tilbagemelding i morgen" (I will get back to you tomorrow).

sentence.da: Chefen gav mig en **tilbagemelding** på rapporten, og den var positiv.
sentence.en: The boss gave me feedback on the report, and it was positive.

en tilbagevenden.explanation: "En tilbagevenden" means "a return". It comes from the verb "at vende tilbage" (to come back). To say where the return is to, add "til" (to): "tilbagevenden til hjemlandet" (the return to the home country).

sentence.da: Folk ventede spændt på musikerens **tilbagevenden** efter ti år.
sentence.en: People waited excitedly for the musician's return after ten years.

en tilbudsavis.explanation: "En tilbudsavis" means "a flyer with offers". It is built from "tilbud" (offer) and "avis" (newspaper). In Denmark, shops deliver these to your mailbox for free.

sentence.da: En **tilbudsavis** viser ugens billige varer.
sentence.en: A flyer with offers shows the week's cheap goods.

en tilføjelse.explanation: "En tilføjelse" means "an addition". It comes from the verb "at tilføje" (to add). To say you add a note, use the verb: "Jeg tilføjer en note" (I add a note).

sentence.da: Den nye **tilføjelse** til huset er et lyst køkken.
sentence.en: The new addition to the house is a bright kitchen.

en tilgang.explanation: "En tilgang" means "an approach". To say what the approach is for, add "til" (to): "en tilgang til undervisning" (an approach to teaching).

sentence.da: Min **tilgang** til problemet er at tage ét skridt ad gangen.
sentence.en: My approach to the problem is to take one step at a time.

en tilhænger.explanation: "En tilhænger" means "a supporter". To say you support a sports team, use "en fan" (a fan): "Jeg er fan af FC København" (I am a fan of FC Copenhagen).

sentence.da: Hun er en stor **tilhænger** af den nye lov.
sentence.en: She is a big supporter of the new law.

en tilhører.explanation: "En tilhører" means "a listener". The same spelling is also the verb "tilhører" (belongs to), from "at tilhøre". For example, "Bogen tilhører mig" (The book belongs to me).

sentence.da: En **tilhører** sidder stille og lytter til foredraget.
sentence.en: A listener sits quietly and listens to the talk.

en tilkørsel.explanation: "En tilkørsel" means "an on-ramp". It is built from "til" (to) and "kørsel" (driving). The opposite is "en afkørsel" (an exit). For example, "Tag afkørsel 12" (Take exit 12).

sentence.da: En **tilkørsel** fører dig op på motorvejen.
sentence.en: An on-ramp leads you up onto the highway.

en tilladelse.explanation: "En tilladelse" means "a permission". When you talk about a document that allows something, use "en tilladelse": "en tilladelse til at fiske" (a permit to fish). When you say you need permission, leave out "en": "Du skal have tilladelse" (You need permission).

sentence.da: Du må ikke bygge uden **tilladelse** fra kommunen.
sentence.en: You may not build without permission from the municipality.

en tilmelding.explanation: "En tilmelding" means "a registration". To say you sign up, use the verb "at tilmelde sig" (to sign up): "Jeg tilmelder mig kurset" (I sign up for the course).

sentence.da: **Tilmelding** er åben indtil fredag.
sentence.en: Sign-up is open until Friday.

en tilpasning.explanation: "En tilpasning" means "an adaptation". It comes from the verb "at tilpasse" (to adapt). To say you adapt a plan, use the verb: "Vi tilpasser planen" (We adapt the plan).

sentence.da: Det kræver **tilpasning** at flytte til et nyt land.
sentence.en: It takes adaptation to move to a new country.

en tilskuer.explanation: "En tilskuer" means "a spectator". To say there are many spectators at a match, use the plural: "Der er mange tilskuere til kampen" (There are many spectators at the match).

sentence.da: En **tilskuer** ser kampen, men spiller ikke selv.
sentence.en: A spectator watches the match but does not play.

en tilstand.explanation: "En tilstand" means "a condition". For a country, do not use it; use "en stat" (a state): "Danmark er en stat" (Denmark is a state).

sentence.da: Bilen er gammel, men den er i god **tilstand**.
sentence.en: The car is old, but it is in good condition.

en tilståelse.explanation: "En tilståelse" means "a confession". It comes from the verb "at tilstå" (to confess). For example, "Han tilstod" (He confessed).

sentence.da: Politiet fik en **tilståelse** efter flere timers afhøring.
sentence.en: The police got a confession after several hours of questioning.

en tiltalt.explanation: "En tiltalt" means "a defendant". To say someone is charged with a crime, use "tiltalt for" (charged with): "Han er tiltalt for tyveri" (He is charged with theft).

sentence.da: I retten sidder en **tiltalt** ved siden af sin forsvarer.
sentence.en: In the courtroom, a defendant sits next to his defense attorney.

en tiltrækning.explanation: "En tiltrækning" means "an attraction", as in the pull between two people. For a place tourists visit, use "en seværdighed" (a sight): "Slottet er en seværdighed" (The castle is a sight).

sentence.da: Der var en stærk **tiltrækning** mellem dem fra første møde.
sentence.en: There was a strong attraction between them from the first meeting.

en tilvænning.explanation: "En tilvænning" means "an adjustment". It comes from the phrase "at vænne sig til" (to get used to): "Jeg vænner mig til byen" (I am getting used to the city).

sentence.da: Det kræver **tilvænning** at starte i en ny børnehave.
sentence.en: It takes some adjustment to start in a new preschool.

en time.explanation: "En time" means "an hour". To say when something happens, use "om" (in): "Vi ses om en time" (See you in an hour). When you talk about a lesson or class, it also means that: "Jeg har en dansktime i dag" (I have a Danish lesson today). For time in general, use "tid" (time): "Jeg har ikke tid" (I do not have time).

sentence.da: Der er tres minutter i en **time**.
sentence.en: There are sixty minutes in an hour.

en ting.explanation: "En ting" means "a thing". To ask about something you do not recognize, say "Hvad er det for en ting?" (What is that thing?)

sentence.da: Jeg har mange **ting** i min taske.
sentence.en: I have many things in my bag.

en titel.explanation: "En titel" means "a title". When you talk about a book, film or song, it is the name on it: "Hvad er filmens titel?" (What is the title of the film?) When you talk about a rank or job name, it also means that: "Hun har titlen professor" (She has the title of professor).

sentence.da: Du kan læse bogens **titel** på forsiden.
sentence.en: You can read the book's title on the cover.

en titelsang.explanation: "En titelsang" means "a theme song". It is built from "en titel" (a title) and "en sang" (a song). To say you sing along, use "synge med" (sing along): "Jeg synger med på titelsangen" (I sing along to the theme song).

sentence.da: Serien starter med en **titelsang**, og jeg synger med.
sentence.en: The series starts with a theme song, and I sing along.

en tjener.explanation: "En tjener" means "a waiter". It comes from the verb "at tjene" (to serve). The same verb also means "to earn". For example, "Hun tjener mange penge" (She earns a lot of money).

sentence.da: En **tjener** bringer maden til bordet.
sentence.en: A waiter brings the food to the table.

en tjeneste.explanation: "En tjeneste" means "a favor or a service". When you ask for help, it means "a favor": "Jeg skylder dig en tjeneste" (I owe you a favor). When you talk about something a company offers, it means "a service": "Banken tilbyder en ny tjeneste" (The bank offers a new service).

sentence.da: Kan du gøre mig en **tjeneste**?
sentence.en: Can you do me a favor?

en toast.explanation: "En toast" means "a toasted sandwich". To order one, say what is in it: "en toast med ost" (a toasted sandwich with cheese). For plain toasted bread, use "ristet brød" (toasted bread): "Jeg vil have ristet brød til morgenmad" (I want toasted bread for breakfast).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have en **toast** med skinke og ost.
sentence.en: I would like a toasted sandwich with ham and cheese.

en togbillet.explanation: "En togbillet" means "a train ticket". It is built from "tog" (train) and "billet" (ticket). To name another kind of ticket, put the vehicle first: "en busbillet" (a bus ticket).

sentence.da: Med en **togbillet** kan du køre med toget.
sentence.en: With a train ticket you can ride the train.

en togfører.explanation: "En togfører" means "a train conductor". The person who drives the train is "en lokomotivfører" (a train driver). For example, "Lokomotivføreren kører toget" (The train driver drives the train).

sentence.da: Vores **togfører** siger, at toget er forsinket.
sentence.en: Our conductor says that the train is delayed.

en togrejse.explanation: "En togrejse" means "a train journey". It is built from "tog" (train) and "rejse" (journey). To say you travel by train, use the verb "at rejse" (to travel): "Jeg rejser med tog" (I travel by train).

sentence.da: Vi ser landet fra vinduet på en **togrejse**.
sentence.en: We see the country from the window on a train journey.

en togstation.explanation: "En togstation" means "a train station". It is built from "tog" (train) and "station" (station). To say where you are, use "på" (at): "Jeg er på togstationen" (I am at the train station).

sentence.da: Vi venter på toget ved en **togstation**.
sentence.en: We wait for the train at a train station.

en toiletbørste.explanation: "En toiletbørste" means "a toilet brush". It is built from "toilet" (toilet) and "børste" (brush). To say where it stands: "Toiletbørsten står ved siden af toilettet" (The toilet brush stands next to the toilet).

sentence.da: Jeg gør toilettet rent med en **toiletbørste**.
sentence.en: I clean the toilet with a toilet brush.

en toldkontrol.explanation: "En toldkontrol" means "a customs check". It is built from "told" (customs) and "kontrol" (check). To say you pass it, use "gå igennem" (go through): "Vi går igennem toldkontrollen" (We go through the customs check).

sentence.da: Vi skal igennem en **toldkontrol** i lufthavnen.
sentence.en: We have to go through a customs check at the airport.

en tolk.explanation: "En tolk" means "an interpreter". Someone who works with written text is "en oversætter" (a translator). For example, "Oversætteren oversætter bogen" (The translator translates the book).

sentence.da: Vi bad en **tolk** om at oversætte, fordi vi ikke talte dansk.
sentence.en: We asked an interpreter to translate because we did not speak Danish.

en tolkning.explanation: "En tolkning" means "an interpretation", as in a reading of a text. When you talk about how an actor plays a role, it also means that: "skuespillerens tolkning af Hamlet" (the actor's interpretation of Hamlet).

sentence.da: Hver læser har sin egen **tolkning** af digtet.
sentence.en: Every reader has their own interpretation of the poem.

en tomat.explanation: "En tomat" means "a tomato". To name food made from tomatoes, put "tomat" in front: "tomatsuppe" (tomato soup) and "tomatsovs" (tomato sauce).

sentence.da: En **tomat** er rød og rund.
sentence.en: A tomato is red and round.

en tombola.explanation: "En tombola" means "a raffle". To say there is a raffle at an event, leave out "en": "Vi har tombola til julefesten" (We have a raffle at the Christmas party). To say you won something in it, use "at vinde" (to win): "Jeg vandt en kage i tombolaen" (I won a cake in the raffle).

sentence.da: Der er **tombola** til festen, og alle kan vinde noget.
sentence.en: There is a raffle at the party, and everyone can win something.

en tommelfinger.explanation: "En tommelfinger" means "a thumb". To say your thumb hurts, use "tommelfingeren" (the thumb): "Jeg har ondt i tommelfingeren" (My thumb hurts, literally "I have pain in the thumb"). To say thumbs up, say "tommelfingeren op".

sentence.da: Din **tommelfinger** er den korteste og tykkeste finger.
sentence.en: Your thumb is the shortest and thickest finger.

en top.explanation: "En top" means "a top", as in clothing. When you talk about the highest point of something, use the same word: "toppen af bjerget" (the top of the mountain).

sentence.da: Det er varmt, og hun tager en **top** på.
sentence.en: It is warm, and she puts on a top.

en torn.explanation: "En torn" means "a thorn". To say something keeps annoying you, use the saying "en torn i øjet" (literally, a thorn in the eye): "Støjen er en torn i øjet på naboerne" (The noise is a thorn in the neighbors' eye).

sentence.da: Rosen har en skarp **torn** på stilken, og den kan stikke.
sentence.en: The rose has a sharp thorn on the stem, and it can prick.

en tornado.explanation: "En tornado" means "a tornado". A much larger system of wind and rain is "en orkan" (a hurricane). For example, "Orkanen kom ind over kysten" (The hurricane came in over the coast).

sentence.da: En **tornado** kan rive huse op og kaste biler gennem luften.
sentence.en: A tornado can tear houses up and throw cars through the air.

en tortilla.explanation: "En tortilla" means "a tortilla". To say what is inside, use "med" (with): "en tortilla med kylling" (a tortilla with chicken).

sentence.da: Jeg fylder en **tortilla** med bønner og ost.
sentence.en: I fill a tortilla with beans and cheese.

en torvehal.explanation: "En torvehal" means "a market hall". It is built from "et torv" (a square) and "en hal" (a hall).

sentence.da: Vi spiser frokost i en **torvehal** i København.
sentence.en: We eat lunch in a market hall in Copenhagen.

en tradition.explanation: "En tradition" means "a tradition". To say you keep one alive, use "at holde fast i" (to hold on to): "Vi holder fast i traditionen" (We hold on to the tradition).

sentence.da: Det er en gammel **tradition** i vores familie.
sentence.en: It is an old tradition in our family.

en tragedie.explanation: "En tragedie" means "a tragedy". When you talk about a play with a sad ending, it also means that: "Hamlet er en tragedie" (Hamlet is a tragedy). The opposite is "en komedie" (a comedy). For example, "Vi så en komedie i går" (We saw a comedy yesterday).

sentence.da: Branden i skolen var en **tragedie** for hele byen.
sentence.en: The fire at the school was a tragedy for the whole town.

en traktat.explanation: "En traktat" means "a treaty". To say countries sign one, use the verb "at underskrive" (to sign): "at underskrive en traktat" (to sign a treaty).

sentence.da: Landene underskrev en **traktat** og lovede at holde freden.
