sentence.en: The countries signed a treaty and promised to keep the peace.

en traktor.explanation: "En traktor" means "a tractor". A person who drives one is "en traktorfører" (a tractor driver), built from "traktor" and "en fører" (a driver).

sentence.da: Landmanden kører **traktor** hen over marken.
sentence.en: The farmer drives a tractor across the field.

en trang.explanation: "En trang" means "an urge". To say what you feel an urge for, add "til" (for): "en trang til sødt" (a craving for sweets). When you describe a narrow room, the describing word "trang" means "narrow": "et trangt rum" (a narrow room).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en pludselig **trang** til at synge.
sentence.en: I suddenly felt an urge to sing.

en transaktion.explanation: "En transaktion" means "a transaction". To say you carry one out, use the verb "at foretage" (to carry out): "at foretage en transaktion" (to carry out a transaction).

sentence.da: Banken har stoppet min **transaktion**, fordi kortet var spærret.
sentence.en: The bank stopped my transaction because the card was blocked.

en trappe.explanation: "En trappe" means "a staircase or stairs". When you walk down the stairs, say "ned ad trappen" (down the stairs): "Jeg går ned ad trappen" (I walk down the stairs).

sentence.da: Der er en **trappe** ned til kælderen.
sentence.en: There is a staircase down to the basement.

en tredjedel.explanation: "En tredjedel" means "a third". It is built from "tredje" (third) and "en del" (a part). To say two thirds, use the plural: "to tredjedele" (two thirds).

sentence.da: Jeg har læst en **tredjedel** af bogen.
sentence.en: I have read a third of the book.

en trekant.explanation: "En trekant" means "a triangle". It is built from "tre" (three) and "en kant" (an edge). For the musical instrument, use "en triangel" (the percussion triangle): "Hun spiller triangel" (She plays the triangle).

sentence.da: Tegn en **trekant** med tre hjørner.
sentence.en: Draw a triangle with three corners.

en tremmeseng.explanation: "En tremmeseng" means "a crib". It is built from "en tremme" (a bar) and "en seng" (a bed).

sentence.da: Den lille sover i en **tremmeseng** ved siden af os.
sentence.en: The little one sleeps in a crib next to us.

en trillebør.explanation: "En trillebør" means "a wheelbarrow". The first part comes from the verb "at trille" (to roll). To say you push a wheelbarrow, use "at skubbe" (to push): "Han skubber trillebøren hen til haven" (He pushes the wheelbarrow to the garden).

sentence.da: Jeg flytter jorden i haven med en **trillebør**.
sentence.en: I move the soil in the garden with a wheelbarrow.

en troldmand.explanation: "En troldmand" means "a wizard". It is built from "en trold" (a troll) and "en mand" (a man).

sentence.da: En **troldmand** kan trylle med en tryllestav.
sentence.en: A wizard can do magic with a magic wand.

en tromme.explanation: "En tromme" means "a drum". A person who plays the drums is "en trommeslager" (a drummer).

sentence.da: Man slår på en **tromme** med to stave.
sentence.en: You hit a drum with two sticks.

en trompet.explanation: "En trompet" means "a trumpet". A person who plays the trumpet is "en trompetist" (a trumpeter).

sentence.da: Min onkel spiller **trompet** i et orkester.
sentence.en: My uncle plays the trumpet in an orchestra.

en trone.explanation: "En trone" means "a throne". When a prince will become king after his father, say "at arve tronen" (to inherit the throne).

sentence.da: Kongen sidder på sin **trone** i den store sal.
sentence.en: The king sits on his throne in the big hall.

en trop.explanation: "En trop" means "a troop". To say a country sends soldiers abroad, use the plural: "Landet sender tropper til udlandet" (The country sends troops abroad).

sentence.da: Hver **trop** af spejdere har sin egen leder.
sentence.en: Each troop of scouts has its own leader.

en trussel.explanation: "En trussel" means "a threat". It is the noun for the verb "at true" (to threaten). To say a threat to something, add "mod" (against): "en trussel mod miljøet" (a threat to the environment).

sentence.da: Det er en **trussel**, når nogen vil gøre dig ondt.
sentence.en: It is a threat when someone wants to hurt you.

en trækfugl.explanation: "En trækfugl" means "a migratory bird". To say a bird stays in Denmark all year, use its opposite, "en standfugl" (a resident bird): "Gråspurven er en standfugl" (The house sparrow is a resident bird).

sentence.da: Svalen er en **trækfugl**, og den flyver til Afrika om vinteren.
sentence.en: The swallow is a migratory bird, and it flies to Africa in the winter.

en træner.explanation: "En træner" means "a coach". It comes from the verb "at træne" (to train). To say whose coach someone is, add "for" (for): "Hun er træner for pigeholdet" (She is the coach of the girls' team).

sentence.da: Vores **træner** er meget god til at forklare.
sentence.en: Our coach is very good at explaining.

en trøje.explanation: "En trøje" means "a sweater". To name a sports shirt, put the sport in front: "en fodboldtrøje" (a soccer jersey).

sentence.da: Jeg har en varm **trøje** på.
sentence.en: I am wearing a warm sweater.

en tudse.explanation: "En tudse" means "a toad". Do not mix it up with "en frø" (a frog). For example, "Der sidder en frø i søen" (A frog is sitting in the lake).

sentence.da: En **tudse** har tør, knoldet hud og lever mest på land.
sentence.en: A toad has dry, bumpy skin and lives mostly on land.

en tulipan.explanation: "En tulipan" means "a tulip". To buy several, ask for "et bundt tulipaner" (a bunch of tulips).

sentence.da: En **tulipan** blomstrer om foråret og kommer fra et løg.
sentence.en: A tulip blooms in spring and grows from a bulb.

en tunge.explanation: "En tunge" means "a tongue". To say you stick out your tongue at someone, say "at række tunge ad nogen" (to stick out your tongue at someone).

sentence.da: Lægen sagde: Vis mig din **tunge**.
sentence.en: The doctor said: Show me your tongue.

en tunnel.explanation: "En tunnel" means "a tunnel". In Aalborg, "Limfjordstunnelen" (the Limfjord tunnel) takes the motorway under the water.

sentence.da: Toget kører gennem en lang **tunnel** under havet.
sentence.en: The train goes through a long tunnel under the sea.

en tur.explanation: "En tur" means "a trip, turn". When you leave home for an outing, say "at tage på tur" (to go on a trip): "Vi tager på tur i weekenden" (We are going on a trip this weekend). When it is your move in a game, say "Det er din tur" (It is your turn).

sentence.da: Vi går en **tur** i parken.
sentence.en: We are going for a walk in the park.

en turist.explanation: "En turist" means "a tourist". A person who lives in a place is "en indbygger" (a resident). For example, "Der bor mange indbyggere i byen" (Many residents live in the city).

sentence.da: Som **turist** vil jeg se hele byen.
sentence.en: As a tourist, I want to see the whole city.

en turistattraktion.explanation: "En turistattraktion" means "a tourist attraction". It is built from "en turist" (a tourist) and "en attraktion" (an attraction).

sentence.da: Den gamle bro er en kendt **turistattraktion**.
sentence.en: The old bridge is a famous tourist attraction.

en turnering.explanation: "En turnering" means "a tournament". To say a team wins one, use the verb "at vinde" (to win): "Holdet vandt turneringen" (The team won the tournament).

sentence.da: Vi skal spille tre kampe i en **turnering** i weekenden.
sentence.en: We will play three matches in a tournament this weekend.

en tusch.explanation: "En tusch" means "a marker". Another name for it is "en tuschpen" (a felt-tip pen), built from "tusch" and "en pen" (a pen).

sentence.da: Børnene tegner med en rød **tusch**.
sentence.en: The children draw with a red marker.

en tv-kanal.explanation: "En tv-kanal" means "a TV channel". To tell someone to change the channel, say "Skift kanal" (Change the channel).

sentence.da: På en **tv-kanal** kan du se programmer.
sentence.en: On a TV channel you can watch programs.

en tv-serie.explanation: "En tv-serie" means "a TV series". To count the parts of a series, use "et afsnit" (an episode): "Vi ser to afsnit i weekenden" (We watch two episodes this weekend).

sentence.da: Jeg ser en ny **tv-serie** om en detektiv.
sentence.en: I am watching a new TV series about a detective.

en tvetydighed.explanation: "En tvetydighed" means "an ambiguity". It is the noun for "tvetydig" (ambiguous). To say something is simply unclear, use "en uklarhed" (a lack of clarity): "Der er en uklarhed i kontrakten" (There is a lack of clarity in the contract).

sentence.da: Sætningen har en **tvetydighed**, fordi man kan læse den på to måder.
sentence.en: The sentence has an ambiguity because you can read it in two ways.

en tvilling.explanation: "En tvilling" means "a twin". To say two people are twins, use the plural: "Min bror og jeg er tvillinger" (My brother and I are twins).

sentence.da: Hun er **tvilling**, og hendes søster ligner hende.
sentence.en: She is a twin, and her sister looks like her.

en tvivl.explanation: "En tvivl" means "a doubt". To say you are certain, use "Der er ingen tvivl" (There is no doubt).

sentence.da: Jeg er i **tvivl** og kan ikke vælge.
sentence.en: I am in doubt and cannot choose.

en type.explanation: "En type" means "a type or guy". To ask what kind of car someone has, say "Hvilken type bil har du?" (What type of car do you have?). To call someone a funny guy, say "en sjov type" (a funny guy).

sentence.da: Han er en meget flink **type**.
sentence.en: He is a very nice guy.

en tyr.explanation: "En tyr" means "a bull". To name the star sign Taurus, use "Tyren" (the Bull): "Jeg er Tyren" (I am Taurus).

sentence.da: En **tyr** er hannen, og en ko er hunnen.
sentence.en: A bull is the male, and a cow is the female.

en tyrekalv.explanation: "En tyrekalv" means "a bull calf". It is built from "en tyr" (a bull) and "en kalv" (a calf). To name a young female, use "en kvie" (a heifer): "Der er en kvie i stalden" (There is a heifer in the barn).

sentence.da: Landmanden har en ko og en **tyrekalv** i stalden.
sentence.en: The farmer has a cow and a bull calf in the barn.

en tyrker.explanation: "En tyrker" means "a Turk". The country is "Tyrkiet" (Turkey). To say something is Turkish, use "tyrkisk" (Turkish): "Jeg elsker tyrkisk mad" (I love Turkish food). Unlike English, Danish does not capitalize nationalities. For example, "en tyrker" (a Turk).

sentence.da: Min nabo er **tyrker**, og han kommer fra Istanbul.
sentence.en: My neighbor is a Turk, and he comes from Istanbul.

en tysker.explanation: "En tysker" means "a German". To say your nationality, use either the noun or the adjective: "Jeg er tysker" and "Jeg er tysk" both mean "I am German".

sentence.da: Hun er **tysker** og bor i Tyskland.
sentence.en: She is German and lives in Germany.

en tyv.explanation: "En tyv" means "a thief". To say someone stole something, use the verb "at stjæle" (to steal): "Han stjal min cykel" (He stole my bike).

sentence.da: En **tyv** har taget min cykel fra gården.
sentence.en: A thief has taken my bike from the yard.

en tå.explanation: "En tå" means "a toe". The big toe is "en storetå" (a big toe), built from "stor" (big) and "en tå" (a toe).

sentence.da: Din **tå** sidder for enden af din fod.
sentence.en: Your toe sits at the end of your foot.

en tåbe.explanation: "En tåbe" means "a fool". To say something was foolish, use "tåbelig" (foolish): "Det var tåbeligt" (That was foolish).

sentence.da: Kun en **tåbe** går ud på den tynde is.
sentence.en: Only a fool walks out on the thin ice.

en tåre.explanation: "En tåre" means "a tear", as in crying. To say someone is close to crying, use "at have tårer i øjnene" (to have tears in your eyes).

sentence.da: Hun græd, og der løb en **tåre** ned ad kinden.
sentence.en: She cried and a tear ran down her cheek.

en tændstik.explanation: "En tændstik" means "a match", as in a stick for lighting a fire. To say a match in sports, use "en kamp" (a game): "Vi ser en kamp i aften" (We are watching a match tonight).

sentence.da: Jeg tænder bålet med en **tændstik**.
sentence.en: I light the fire with a match.

en tærskel.explanation: "En tærskel" means "a threshold", as in the bottom of a doorway. To say how much pain someone can take, use "en smertetærskel" (a pain threshold): "Hun har en høj smertetærskel" (She has a high pain threshold).

sentence.da: Det lave stykke i gulvet under en døråbning er en **tærskel**.
sentence.en: The low piece in the floor under a doorway is a threshold.

en tøjbutik.explanation: "En tøjbutik" means "a clothing store". It is built from "tøj" (clothes) and "en butik" (a shop). Other shops are named the same way, such as "en skobutik" (a shoe store).

sentence.da: Jeg køber bukser i en **tøjbutik**.
sentence.en: I buy pants in a clothing store.

en tøjbøjle.explanation: "En tøjbøjle" means "a clothes hanger". It is built from "tøj" (clothes) and "en bøjle" (a hanger).

sentence.da: Skjorten hænger på en **tøjbøjle** i skabet.
sentence.en: The shirt hangs on a clothes hanger in the closet.

en tøjkurv.explanation: "En tøjkurv" means "a laundry basket". It is built from "tøj" (clothes) and "en kurv" (a basket).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger de beskidte sokker i min **tøjkurv**.
sentence.en: I put the dirty socks in my laundry basket.

en tøjstørrelse.explanation: "En tøjstørrelse" means "a clothing size". It is built from "tøj" (clothes) and "en størrelse" (a size). To ask a shop for a bigger size, say "Har I den i en større størrelse?" (Do you have it in a larger size?).

sentence.da: Min **tøjstørrelse** er M, men jeg vil gerne prøve L.
sentence.en: My clothing size is M, but I would like to try L.

en tøjvask.explanation: "En tøjvask" means "a laundry", as in one load of clothes you wash. The business that washes clothes for you is "et vaskeri" (a laundry). For example, "Jeg afleverer dynen på vaskeriet" (I drop the duvet off at the laundry).

sentence.da: Jeg skal lave en **tøjvask**, fordi kurven er fuld.
sentence.en: I need to do a load of laundry because the basket is full.

en tømrer.explanation: "En tømrer" means "a carpenter". To name the person who makes furniture, use "en snedker" (a cabinetmaker): "Snedkeren laver et nyt bord" (The cabinetmaker makes a new table).

sentence.da: Min onkel er **tømrer** og arbejder med træ.
sentence.en: My uncle is a carpenter and works with wood.

en tønde.explanation: "En tønde" means "a barrel". At Fastelavn, Danish children hit a barrel and the saying is "at slå katten af tønden" (to knock the cat out of the barrel).

sentence.da: Vinen modner i en **tønde** af egetræ i kælderen.
sentence.en: The wine ages in an oak barrel in the cellar.

en tørke.explanation: "En tørke" means "a drought". It is the noun for the describing word "tør" (dry).

sentence.da: Landmændene mister afgrøder, når en **tørke** varer i flere måneder.
sentence.en: Farmers lose crops when a drought lasts for several months.

en tørresnor.explanation: "En tørresnor" means "a clothesline". It is built from "tørre" (dry) and "en snor" (a cord).

sentence.da: Jeg hænger vasketøjet op på en **tørresnor**.
sentence.en: I hang the laundry up on a clothesline.

en tørretumbler.explanation: "En tørretumbler" means "a dryer", as in the machine for clothes. To dry clothes outside, use "en tørresnor" (a clothesline): "Tøjet hænger på tørresnoren" (The clothes hang on the clothesline).

sentence.da: Vi har ikke en **tørretumbler**, så tøjet hænger ude.
sentence.en: We do not have a dryer, so the clothes hang outside.

en tøven.explanation: "En tøven" means "a hesitation". It comes from the verb "at tøve" (to hesitate). To say you did something without hesitating, say "uden tøven" (without hesitation): "Han svarede uden tøven" (He answered without hesitation).

sentence.da: Hun sagde ja uden **tøven**, fordi hun var helt sikker.
sentence.en: She said yes without hesitation because she was completely sure.

et tag.explanation: "Et tag" means "a roof". When you tell someone to take something, the command "Tag!" (Take!) is spelled the same: "Tag en kage!" (Take a cake!)

sentence.da: Huset har et rødt **tag**.
sentence.en: The house has a red roof.

en takeaway.explanation: "En takeaway" means "a takeout meal". To say you collect your order, use the verb "at hente" (to pick up): "Jeg henter vores takeaway" (I am picking up our takeout).

sentence.da: Vi bestiller **takeaway** i aften, fordi vi er trætte.
sentence.en: We are ordering takeout tonight because we are tired.

et takkekort.explanation: "Et takkekort" means "a thank-you card". It is built from "en tak" (a thanks) and "et kort" (a card).

sentence.da: Hun skrev et **takkekort** til sin lærer, fordi han hjalp hende.
sentence.en: She wrote a thank-you card to her teacher because he helped her.

et tal.explanation: "Et tal" means "a number", as in a figure like 5 or 12. For a phone or house number, use "et nummer" (a number): "Hvad er dit nummer?" (What is your number?)

sentence.da: Fem er et lille **tal**.
sentence.en: Five is a small number.

et talent.explanation: "Et talent" means "a talent". To say a person has talent, use the describing word "talentfuld" (talented): "Han er meget talentfuld" (He is very talented).

sentence.da: Hun har et stort **talent** for musik.
sentence.en: She has a great talent for music.

et talkshow.explanation: "Et talkshow" means "a talk show". To name the person who leads a talk show, use "en vært" (a host): "Værten stiller svære spørgsmål" (The host asks hard questions).

sentence.da: Skuespilleren var gæst i et **talkshow** i går aftes.
sentence.en: The actor was a guest on a talk show last night.

et tandkrus.explanation: "Et tandkrus" means "a toothbrush cup". It is built from "en tand" (a tooth) and "et krus" (a mug).

sentence.da: Jeg putter tandbørsten i et blåt **tandkrus**.
sentence.en: I put the toothbrush in a blue toothbrush cup.

et tastatur.explanation: "Et tastatur" means "a keyboard", as in the one on a computer. To say you press a key on it, use "en tast" (a key): "Tryk på en tast" (Press a key). For a key to a door, use "en nøgle" (a key): "Jeg har glemt min nøgle" (I forgot my key).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver hurtigt på mit nye **tastatur**.
sentence.en: I type fast on my new keyboard.

et team.explanation: "Et team" means "a team", as in a group working together. To name a sports team, use "et hold" (a team): "Vores hold vandt i går" (Our team won yesterday).

sentence.da: Mit **team** arbejder sammen om et nyt projekt.
sentence.en: My team is working together on a new project.

et teater.explanation: "Et teater" means "a theater". To say you go to the movies instead, use "en biograf" (a movie theater): "Vi går i biografen i aften" (We are going to the movies tonight).

sentence.da: Vi ser et skuespil i et stort **teater** i aften.
sentence.en: We are watching a play in a big theater tonight.

et teaterstykke.explanation: "Et teaterstykke" means "a stage play". It is built from "et teater" (a theater) and "et stykke" (a piece).

sentence.da: Et **teaterstykke** bliver spillet live foran et publikum.
sentence.en: A stage play is performed live in front of an audience.

et tegn.explanation: "Et tegn" means "a sign", as in a hint of what will happen. For example, "Sorte skyer er et tegn på regn" (Black clouds are a sign of rain). For a sign you read on a door or a shop, use "et skilt" (a signboard): "Der hænger et skilt på døren" (A sign hangs on the door).

sentence.da: Hendes smil er et godt **tegn**.
sentence.en: Her smile is a good sign.

et telefonnummer.explanation: "Et telefonnummer" means "a phone number". It is built from "telefon" (phone) and "et nummer" (a number), the same "nummer" as in "et husnummer" (a house number).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til ham på hans **telefonnummer**.
sentence.en: I call him on his phone number.

et telt.explanation: "Et telt" means "a tent". To say you put one up, use "at slå op" (to pitch): "Vi slår teltet op ved søen" (We pitch the tent by the lake).

sentence.da: Vi sover i et **telt** i weekenden.
sentence.en: We are sleeping in a tent this weekend.

et tema.explanation: "Et tema" means "a theme". The word is also part of "en temadag" (a day built around one theme). For example, "Skolen holder en temadag om miljø" (The school holds a theme day about the environment).

sentence.da: Bogens **tema** er venskab og tab.
sentence.en: The theme of the book is friendship and loss.

et tempel.explanation: "Et tempel" means "a temple". For a Christian place of worship, use "en kirke" (a church): "Vi gifter os i kirken" (We are getting married at the church).

sentence.da: Munkene beder i et **tempel** hver morgen.
sentence.en: The monks pray in a temple every morning.

et temperament.explanation: "Et temperament" means "a temper or temperament". To describe a hot temper, add "hidsigt" (fiery): "et hidsigt temperament" (a fiery temperament).

sentence.da: Hans **temperament** er så livligt, at han aldrig sidder stille.
sentence.en: His temperament is so lively that he never sits still.

et termometer.explanation: "Et termometer" means "a thermometer". To say you check someone's temperature, use "at tage temperaturen på" (to take the temperature of): "Jeg tager temperaturen på barnet" (I take the child's temperature).

sentence.da: Jeg henter et **termometer**, fordi jeg har feber.
sentence.en: I get a thermometer because I have a fever.

et territorium.explanation: "Et territorium" means "a territory". The sea that belongs to a country is "territorialfarvand" (territorial waters). For example, "Skibet sejler i dansk territorialfarvand" (The ship sails in Danish territorial waters).

sentence.da: Dyret forsvarer sit **territorium** mod andre dyr.
sentence.en: The animal defends its territory against other animals.

et testamente.explanation: "Et testamente" means "a will or testament". To say you write a will, use "at skrive testamente" (to write a will): "Min bedstefar har skrevet testamente" (My grandfather has written a will). For the part of the Bible, use "Det Nye Testamente" (the New Testament).

sentence.da: Hun skrev i sit **testamente**, at børnene skal arve huset.
sentence.en: She wrote in her will that the children are to inherit the house.

et tidsfordriv.explanation: "Et tidsfordriv" means "a pastime". It comes from "at fordrive tiden" (to pass the time). For example, "Jeg fordriver tiden med at læse" (I pass the time by reading).

sentence.da: Et krydsord er et godt **tidsfordriv** på en lang togtur.
sentence.en: A crossword is a good pastime on a long train ride.

et tidspunkt.explanation: "Et tidspunkt" means "a point in time". To say "at that time", use "på det tidspunkt" (at that time): "På det tidspunkt var jeg hjemme" (At that time I was at home).

sentence.da: Hvilket **tidspunkt** passer dig bedst?
sentence.en: Which time suits you best?

et tidsrum.explanation: "Et tidsrum" means "a period of time". To say between which times, use "i tidsrummet mellem" (in the period between): "i tidsrummet mellem otte og ti" (in the period between eight and ten). For one exact moment, use "et tidspunkt" (a point in time): "Hvilket tidspunkt passer dig?" (Which time suits you?)

sentence.da: Der er et **tidsrum** på en time, hvor butikken er lukket.
sentence.en: There is a period of one hour when the store is closed.

et tilbageslag.explanation: "Et tilbageslag" means "a setback". It is built from "tilbage" (back) and "et slag" (a blow). To say you suffer one, use "at få" (to get): "Han fik et tilbageslag i sin bedring" (He suffered a setback in his recovery).

sentence.da: Fabrikkens lukning var et stort **tilbageslag** for hele byen.
sentence.en: The closing of the factory was a big setback for the whole town.

et tilbud.explanation: "Et tilbud" means "an offer or deal". To say a shop sells something cheaper for a while, use "på tilbud" (on sale): "Kaffen er på tilbud" (The coffee is on sale).

sentence.da: Kaffe til 20 kroner er et godt **tilbud**.
sentence.en: Coffee for 20 kroner is a good deal.

et tilbudskatalog.explanation: "Et tilbudskatalog" means "a sale catalog". It is built from "et tilbud" (an offer) and "et katalog" (a catalog).

sentence.da: Jeg kigger i et **tilbudskatalog** og finder billig mad.
sentence.en: I look in a sale catalog and find cheap food.

et tilfælde.explanation: "Et tilfælde" means "a case or coincidence". To say something happened by chance, use "ved et tilfælde" (by chance): "Jeg mødte hende ved et tilfælde" (I met her by chance). For a case in court, use "en sag" (a case): "Sagen kommer for retten i morgen" (The case goes to court tomorrow).

sentence.da: I dette **tilfælde** må vi vente.
sentence.en: In this case we have to wait.

et tilholdssted.explanation: "Et tilholdssted" means "a hangout or haunt". It is built from "at holde til" (to stay somewhere regularly) and "et sted" (a place).

sentence.da: Biblioteket er de unges faste **tilholdssted** efter skole.
sentence.en: The library is the young people's regular hangout after school.

et tillægsord.explanation: "Et tillægsord" means "an adjective". It is built from "et tillæg" (an addition) and "et ord" (a word). Another word for it is "et adjektiv" (an adjective).

sentence.da: Ordet stor er et **tillægsord**, fordi det beskriver en ting.
sentence.en: The word stor is an adjective because it describes a thing.

et tiltag.explanation: "Et tiltag" means "an initiative or measure". To say what a step is aimed at, add "mod" (against): "nye tiltag mod trafikstøj" (new measures against traffic noise).

sentence.da: Byen indfører et nyt **tiltag**: gratis bus for børn.
sentence.en: The city is introducing a new initiative: free buses for children.

et tip.explanation: "Et tip" means "a tip", as in a helpful suggestion. To say you leave money for service, use "drikkepenge" (tip money): "Vi gav tjeneren drikkepenge" (We gave the waiter a tip).

sentence.da: Min lærer gav mig et godt **tip** til eksamen.
sentence.en: My teacher gave me a good tip for the exam.

et tog.explanation: "Et tog" means "a train". To say you travel by train, use "med toget" (by train): "Jeg rejser med toget" (I travel by train). The same spelling is also the past tense of "at tage" (to take). For example, "Han tog min bog" (He took my book).

sentence.da: Vi tager et **tog** til København.
sentence.en: We take a train to Copenhagen.

et toilet.explanation: "Et toilet" means "a toilet". To ask where the restroom is, say "Hvor er toilettet?" (Where is the toilet?)

sentence.da: Jeg skal på **toilet** og vaske hænder.
sentence.en: I am going to the restroom to wash my hands.

et topmøde.explanation: "Et topmøde" means "a summit". It is built from "en top" (a top) and "et møde" (a meeting).

sentence.da: Lederne mødes til et **topmøde** om klimaet i næste uge.
sentence.en: The leaders meet at a summit about the climate next week.

et tordenvejr.explanation: "Et tordenvejr" means "a thunderstorm". It is built from "torden" (thunder) and "vejr" (weather), the same "vejr" as in "regnvejr" (rainy weather) and "solskinsvejr" (sunny weather).

sentence.da: Vi bliver inde, fordi der er **tordenvejr**.
sentence.en: We are staying inside because there is a thunderstorm.

et torv.explanation: "Et torv" means "a square", as in an open space in a town.

sentence.da: Man kan købe frugt og grønt på et **torv**.
sentence.en: You can buy fruit and vegetables at a market square.

et trafiklys.explanation: "Et trafiklys" means "a traffic light". It is built from "trafik" (traffic) and "et lys" (a light). When you mean a candle, "et lys" works too: "et lys på bordet" (a candle on the table).

sentence.da: Bilerne stopper ved et rødt **trafiklys**.
sentence.en: The cars stop at a red traffic light.

et trick.explanation: "Et trick" means "a trick". To say you do a trick, use "at lave" (to do, to make): "Han laver et trick med en mønt" (He does a trick with a coin).

sentence.da: Hunden lærer et nyt **trick**, og børnene klapper.
sentence.en: The dog learns a new trick, and the kids clap.

et trin.explanation: "Et trin" means "a step", as in one stair of a staircase or one stage in a process. For a step you take with your foot, use "et skridt" (a step): "Tag et skridt frem" (Take a step forward).

sentence.da: Vi tager det næste **trin** i planen.
sentence.en: We take the next step in the plan.

et tryk.explanation: "Et tryk" means "a pressure or stress". To say you press a button, use "et tryk på knappen" (a press on the button). In "blodtryk" (blood pressure), "tryk" means "pressure".

sentence.da: Man lægger **tryk** på første del af ordet.
sentence.en: You put stress on the first part of the word.

et træ.explanation: "Et træ" means "a tree". To say what something is made of, use "træ" (wood) after "af" (of): "et bord af træ" (a table made of wood). For a large group of trees, use "en skov" (a forest): "Vi går en tur i skoven" (We go for a walk in the forest).

sentence.da: Æbler vokser på et **træ**.
sentence.en: Apples grow on a tree.

et træk.explanation: "Et træk" means "a move". To praise a clever move, say "Det var et smart træk" (That was a smart move). To say cold air blows through a room, use "træk" (a draft): "Der er træk i stuen" (There is a draft in the room).

sentence.da: Det næste **træk** i skak kan afgøre hele spillet.
sentence.en: The next move in chess can decide the whole game.

et træningspas.explanation: "Et træningspas" means "a training session". To talk about exercising in general, use "træning" (training): "Træning er sundt" (Exercise is healthy).

sentence.da: Jeg har et **træningspas** hver tirsdag og torsdag.
sentence.en: I have a training session every Tuesday and Thursday.

et tv.explanation: "Et tv" means "a TV". To say you watch TV, use "at se tv" (literally, "to see TV").

sentence.da: Jeg sidder i sofaen og ser **tv**.
sentence.en: I sit on the sofa and watch TV.

et tv-program.explanation: "Et tv-program" means "a TV program". For a show with many episodes, use "en tv-serie" (a TV series): "Jeg ser en tv-serie om en detektiv" (I watch a TV series about a detective).

sentence.da: Der kommer et godt **tv-program** i aften.
sentence.en: A good TV program is coming on tonight.

et tyveri.explanation: "Et tyveri" means "a theft". It comes from "en tyv" (a thief). To say you report a theft, use "at anmelde" (to report): "Jeg vil gerne anmelde et tyveri" (I would like to report a theft).

sentence.da: Politiet kommer, fordi der er sket et **tyveri**.
sentence.en: The police are coming because a theft has happened.

et tårn.explanation: "Et tårn" means "a tower". In chess, "et tårn" is also the piece called a rook. For example, "Jeg flytter mit tårn" (I move my rook).

sentence.da: Der er en flot udsigt fra det høje **tårn**.
sentence.en: There is a nice view from the tall tower.

et tæppe.explanation: "Et tæppe" means "a rug or blanket". It is a rug when it lies on the floor and a blanket when you lay it over yourself. It is also part of "et gulvtæppe" (a floor rug), built from "et gulv" (a floor) and "tæppe".

sentence.da: Jeg lægger et **tæppe** over benene.
sentence.en: I put a blanket over my legs.

et tørklæde.explanation: "Et tørklæde" means "a scarf". The second part is "klæde" (cloth), the same part as in "et håndklæde" (a towel).

sentence.da: Jeg har et **tørklæde** om halsen.
sentence.en: I have a scarf around my neck.

et tørrestativ.explanation: "Et tørrestativ" means "a drying rack". It is built from "at tørre" (to dry) and "et stativ" (a stand). The same "stativ" is in "et cykelstativ" (a bike rack).

sentence.da: Jeg hænger tøjet på mit **tørrestativ**.
sentence.en: I hang the clothes on my drying rack.

tag det roligt.explanation: "Tag det roligt" means "take it easy". To say goodbye to a friend, you can end with it: "Vi ses i morgen, tag det roligt" (See you tomorrow, take it easy).

forms.en: You have to take it easy

sentence.da: **Tag det roligt**, vi kommer ikke for sent.
sentence.en: Take it easy, we will not be late.

tak.explanation: "Tak" means "thanks". When you accept an offer, say "ja tak" (yes, please). When you order, put it after the item: "Kaffe, tak" (Coffee, please). To answer someone who thanks you, say "selv tak" (you're welcome).

sentence.da: **Tak** for maden!
sentence.en: Thanks for the food!

tak for det.explanation: "Tak for det" means "thanks for that". To name what you are thanking the person for, put it after "tak for" (thanks for): "Tak for kaffen" (Thanks for the coffee).

sentence.da: Her er din kaffe. **Tak for det**!
sentence.en: Here is your coffee. Thanks for that!

tak for i dag.explanation: "Tak for i dag" means "thanks for today". You say it when you part after a day together, such as at work or on a course. To thank someone for another day, swap "i dag" (today) for that day: "Tak for i går" (Thanks for yesterday).

forms.da: Tak for i dag, vi ses.

sentence.da: Vi ses i morgen. **Tak for i dag**!
sentence.en: See you tomorrow. Thanks for today!

tak for mad.explanation: "Tak for mad" means "thanks for the meal". Literally, it is "thanks for food", since "mad" means "food". You say it at the end of a meal to thank whoever made the food. To answer, the cook says "velbekomme" (you're welcome, said about food).

forms.da: Tak for mad, det var lækkert.
forms.en: Thanks for the meal, it was delicious.

sentence.da: Maden var lækker. **Tak for mad**!
sentence.en: The food was delicious. Thanks for the meal!

tak for sidst.explanation: "Tak for sidst" means "thanks for last time". The word "sidst" means "last". You say it when you meet someone again after an earlier get-together: "Hej Anna, tak for sidst!" (Hi Anna, thanks for last time!).

forms.da: Tak for sidst, det var hyggeligt.
forms.en: Thanks for last time, that was nice.

sentence.da: **Tak for sidst**, det var en dejlig aften.
sentence.en: Thanks for last time, it was a lovely evening.

taknemmelig.explanation: "Taknemmelig" means "grateful". It contains "tak" (thanks). To name what you are grateful for, use "for" (for): "Hun var taknemmelig for gaven" (She was grateful for the gift).

sentence.da: Jeg er så **taknemmelig** for din hjælp.
sentence.en: I am so grateful for your help.

taknemmelighed.explanation: "Taknemmelighed" means "gratitude". It is built from "taknemmelig" (grateful) plus the ending "-hed", which turns an adjective into a noun, as in "frihed" (freedom) from "fri" (free).

sentence.da: Han sendte blomster som tegn på **taknemmelighed**.
sentence.en: He sent flowers as a sign of gratitude.

tal langsomt.explanation: "Tal langsomt" means "speak slowly". "Tal" is the command form of "at tale" (to speak), and "langsomt" means "slowly". To ask politely, add "tak" (please) at the end.

forms.da: Jeg forstår, når du taler langsomt.
forms.en: I understand when you speak slowly.

sentence.da: Jeg er ny her. **Tal langsomt**, tak.
sentence.en: I am new here. Speak slowly, please.

talentfuld.explanation: "Talentfuld" means "talented". It is built from "et talent" (a talent) and "-fuld" (full of), the same "-fuld" as in "meningsfuld" (meaningful).

sentence.da: Han er en meget **talentfuld** fodboldspiller.
sentence.en: He is a very talented soccer player.

taler du engelsk?.explanation: "Taler du engelsk?" means "Do you speak English?". When you ask one person, use "du" (you). When you ask several people, use "I" (you all): "Taler I engelsk?" (Do you all speak English?).

forms.en: I only speak a little Danish.

sentence.da: Undskyld, **taler du engelsk?**
sentence.en: Excuse me, do you speak English?

tandpasta.explanation: "Tandpasta" means "a toothpaste". It is built from "tand" (tooth) and "pasta" (paste), and it takes "en".

sentence.da: Der er ikke mere **tandpasta** i tuben.
sentence.en: There is no more toothpaste in the tube.

tandpine.explanation: "Tandpine" means "a toothache". It is built from "tand" (tooth) and "pine" (pain). To say it another way, use "Jeg har ondt i tanden" (I have a toothache; literally, "I have pain in the tooth").

sentence.da: Jeg har **tandpine** og skal til tandlægen.
sentence.en: I have a toothache and need to go to the dentist.

tandtråd.explanation: "Tandtråd" means "dental floss". It is built from "tand" (tooth) and "en tråd" (a thread).

sentence.da: Efter maden bruger jeg **tandtråd** mellem tænderne.
sentence.en: After the meal I use dental floss between my teeth.

tankefuld.explanation: "Tankefuld" means "pensive". It is built from "en tanke" (a thought) and "-fuld" (full of). To say someone is kind and considerate, use "omtænksom" (considerate): "Det var omtænksomt af dig" (That was considerate of you).

sentence.da: Han blev **tankefuld** og stirrede længe ud af vinduet.
sentence.en: He became pensive and stared out of the window for a long time.

tankeløs.explanation: "Tankeløs" means "thoughtless". It is built from "en tanke" (a thought) and "-løs" (without), the same "-løs" as in "hjemløs" (homeless).

sentence.da: Han er **tankeløs** og tænker aldrig på andre.
sentence.en: He is thoughtless and never thinks about others.

tape.explanation: "Tape" means "tape". For double-sided tape, say "dobbeltklæbende tape".

sentence.da: Jeg klistrer plakaten op med **tape**.
sentence.en: I stick the poster up with tape.

tapet.explanation: "Tapet" means "wallpaper". It takes "et", as the form "tapetet" (the wallpaper) shows.

sentence.da: Der er gammelt **tapet** på væggen.
sentence.en: There is old wallpaper on the wall.

tatoveret.explanation: "Tatoveret" means "tattooed". It comes from "at tatovere" (to tattoo).

sentence.da: Hans arm er **tatoveret** med en stor drage.
sentence.en: His arm is tattooed with a big dragon.

tavs.explanation: "Tavs" means "silent". To describe a calm place without noise, use "stille" (quiet): "et stille rum" (a quiet room).

sentence.da: Hun var **tavs** og sagde ikke et ord.
sentence.en: She was silent and did not say a word.

te.explanation: "Te" means "a tea". It is said like English "tay". Do not mix it up with "ti" (ten), which is said like "tee". For example, "ti kopper te" (ten cups of tea).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker varm **te** med citron.
sentence.en: I drink hot tea with lemon.

tegnsætning.explanation: "Tegnsætning" means "punctuation". It is built from "et tegn" (a mark) and "at sætte" (to put).

sentence.da: God **tegnsætning** gør det lettere at læse en tekst.
sentence.en: Good punctuation makes it easier to read a text.

teknisk.explanation: "Teknisk" means "technical". To say "technically speaking", use "teknisk set": "Teknisk set er det muligt" (Technically speaking, it is possible).

sentence.da: Der er en **teknisk** fejl i systemet.
sentence.en: There is a technical error in the system.

temmelig.explanation: "Temmelig" means "rather". To say how sure you are, put it before "sikker" (sure): "Jeg er temmelig sikker" (I am rather sure).

sentence.da: Vejret er **temmelig** koldt for juni.
sentence.en: The weather is rather cold for June.

tennis.explanation: "Tennis" means "tennis". It goes with the verb "at spille" (to play). For example, "Vi spiller tennis hver søndag" (We play tennis every Sunday).

sentence.da: I **tennis** slår man bolden over nettet.
sentence.en: In tennis, you hit the ball over the net.

teoretisk.explanation: "Teoretisk" means "theoretical". To say "in theory", use "teoretisk set": "Teoretisk set kan det lade sig gøre" (Theoretically, it can be done).

sentence.da: Bogen er **teoretisk** og forklarer ideer uden eksempler.
sentence.en: The book is theoretical and explains ideas without examples.

terapi.explanation: "Terapi" means "a therapy". The person who gives it is "en terapeut" (a therapist).

sentence.da: Hun går i **terapi** hver uge.
sentence.en: She goes to therapy every week.

ternet.explanation: "Ternet" means "checkered". To say squared paper, use "ternet papir" (squared paper).

sentence.da: Dugen på bordet er rød og hvid og **ternet**.
sentence.en: The cloth on the table is red and white and checkered.

terrorisme.explanation: "Terrorisme" means "terrorism". The ending "-isme" is the same as English "-ism", as in "kapitalisme" (capitalism).

sentence.da: Mange lande samarbejder om at bekæmpe **terrorisme**.
sentence.en: Many countries work together to fight terrorism.

ti.explanation: "Ti" means "ten", said like "tee". Do not mix it up with "tid" (time), which ends in "d". For example, "Jeg har ikke tid" (I do not have time).

sentence.da: Efter ni kommer **ti**.
sentence.en: After nine comes ten.

tidevand.explanation: "Et tidevand" means "a tide". It is built from "tid" (time) and "vand" (water). The high point is "højvande" (high tide), and the low point is "lavvande" (low tide).

sentence.da: Når vandet går ud og kommer ind igen, kalder vi det **tidevand**.
sentence.en: When the water goes out and comes in again, we call that the tide.

tidlig.explanation: "Tidlig" means "early". To say you do something early, use "tidligt" (early) instead: "Jeg står tidligt op" (I get up early).

sentence.da: Du er **tidlig** til mødet.
sentence.en: You are early for the meeting.

tidligere.explanation: "Tidligere" means "earlier". To say something happened before now, use it after the verb: "Vi sås tidligere" (We met earlier). To name a past role, put it before the role to mean "former": "en tidligere elev" (a former student).

sentence.da: Hun har **tidligere** boet i Aarhus.
sentence.en: She has previously lived in Aarhus.

tidligt.explanation: "Tidligt" means "early". To say you do something early, put it after the verb: "Vi kom tidligt" (We came early). To describe a thing as early, use "tidlig" (early) instead: "en tidlig morgen" (an early morning).

sentence.da: Jeg står **tidligt** op klokken fem.
sentence.en: I get up early at five o'clock.

tidskrævende.explanation: "Tidskrævende" means "time-consuming". It is built from "tid" (time) and "krævende" (demanding).

sentence.da: Det er **tidskrævende** at skrive en lang rapport.
sentence.en: It is time-consuming to write a long report.

tidspres.explanation: "Et tidspres" means "a time pressure". It is built from "tid" (time) and "et pres" (a pressure).

sentence.da: Det blev ikke færdigt på grund af **tidspres**.
sentence.en: It was not finished because of time pressure.

tidssvarende.explanation: "Tidssvarende" means "up-to-date". It is built from "en tid" (a time) and "svarende" (matching). To say information is current, use "opdateret" (updated): "Siden er opdateret" (The page is updated).

sentence.da: Reglerne er gamle og ikke længere **tidssvarende**.
sentence.en: The rules are old and no longer up to date.

tiende.explanation: "Tiende" means "tenth". To say a date, use "den tiende juni" (the tenth of June), which is written "10. juni" with a dot after the number.

sentence.da: Efter den niende kommer den **tiende**.
sentence.en: After the ninth comes the tenth.

til.explanation: "Til" means "to". To say where you are going, put it before the place: "Toget kører til København" (The train goes to Copenhagen). To say who something is for, it means "for": "Gaven er til dig" (The gift is for you). To say what a meal is for, use "til morgenmad" (for breakfast). To say when at a holiday, use "til jul" (at Christmas).

sentence.da: Jeg rejser **til** Aarhus i morgen.
sentence.en: I am traveling to Aarhus tomorrow.

til fælles.explanation: "Til fælles" means "in common". It goes with "at have" (to have). For example, "at have noget til fælles" (to have something in common).

forms.en: What do you have in common?

sentence.da: Vi har mange ting **til fælles**.
sentence.en: We have many things in common.

til gengæld.explanation: "Til gengæld" means "on the other hand". To add a good side to something bad, use it after "men" (but): "Huset er lille, men til gengæld er det billigt" (The house is small, but on the other hand it is cheap). It also means "in return". For example, "Jeg laver mad, og til gengæld tager du opvasken" (I cook, and in return you do the dishes).

forms.da: Det er dyrt, men til gengæld godt.
forms.en: It is expensive, but on the other hand it is good.

forms.da: Bilen er gammel, men til gengæld billig.
forms.en: The car is old, but on the other hand it is cheap.

sentence.da: Lejligheden er lille, men **til gengæld** ligger den centralt.
sentence.en: The apartment is small, but on the other hand it is centrally located.

til højre.explanation: "Til højre" means "to the right". To give a direction, say: "Vi skal køre til højre ved bageren" (We have to turn right at the bakery). To say where something is, say: "Kaffen står til højre" (The coffee is on the right).

forms.en: The bank is on the right.

sentence.da: Min skole ligger **til højre** for kirken.
sentence.en: My school is to the right of the church.

til sidst.explanation: "Til sidst" means "finally or in the end". Literally, it is "to last", since "sidst" means "last". To say what happened after everything else, use it at the start: "Til sidst blev det mørkt" (In the end it got dark).

forms.en: In the end we went home.

sentence.da: Vi spiste middag, og **til sidst** drak vi kaffe.
sentence.en: We had dinner, and finally we drank coffee.

til tiden.explanation: "Til tiden" means "on time". Literally, it is "to the time". To tell someone to arrive on time, use it with "at komme" (to come): "Kom til tiden!" (Come on time!).

sentence.da: Bussen kom **til tiden**, og vi kom ikke for sent.
sentence.en: The bus came on time, and we were not late.

til venstre.explanation: "Til venstre" means "to the left". To give a direction, say: "Drej til venstre" (Turn left). To say where something is, say: "Bordet står til venstre" (The table is on the left).

forms.en: The post office is on the left.

sentence.da: Hjertet sidder **til venstre** i brystet.
sentence.en: The heart is on the left in the chest.

tilbage.explanation: "Tilbage" means "back". To say someone returns, put it after the verb: "Hun går tilbage" (She goes back). It also means "left over". For example, "Der er to tilbage" (There are two left). For the back of your body, use "en ryg" (a back) instead: "Jeg har ondt i ryggen" (My back hurts).

sentence.da: Jeg kommer snart **tilbage**.
sentence.en: I will be back soon.

tilfreds.explanation: "Tilfreds" means "satisfied". To name what you are satisfied with, add "med" (with): "Jeg er tilfreds med resultatet" (I am satisfied with the result).

sentence.da: Kunden er **tilfreds** med maden.
sentence.en: The customer is satisfied with the food.

tilfreds med.explanation: "Tilfreds med" means "satisfied with". To say the opposite, use "utilfreds med" (dissatisfied with): "Kunden er utilfreds med servicen" (The customer is dissatisfied with the service).

forms.da: Jeg er tilfreds med min lejlighed.
forms.en: I am satisfied with my apartment.
Are you satisfied with the food?
We are satisfied with the house.

sentence.da: Jeg er **tilfreds med** mit nye job.
sentence.en: I am satisfied with my new job.

tilfredshed.explanation: "Tilfredshed" means "satisfaction". The ending "-hed" turns an adjective into a noun, as in "frihed" (freedom) from "fri" (free). To say customer satisfaction, put "kunde" (customer) in front: "kundetilfredshed" (customer satisfaction).

sentence.da: Hun så på sit arbejde med **tilfredshed**.
sentence.en: She looked at her work with satisfaction.

tilfredsstillende.explanation: "Tilfredsstillende" means "satisfying". It comes from "at tilfredsstille" (to satisfy). It also means "satisfactory", meaning good enough. For example, "Resultaterne er tilfredsstillende" (The results are satisfactory).

sentence.da: Resultatet var **tilfredsstillende**, og alle var glade.
sentence.en: The result was satisfactory, and everyone was happy.

tilfældig.explanation: "Tilfældig" means "random". To describe something that happens by chance, use it before the thing: "et tilfældigt møde" (a chance meeting). To say you happened to do something, use "tilfældigvis" (by chance): "Jeg mødte ham tilfældigvis" (I happened to meet him).

sentence.da: Jeg valgte en **tilfældig** bog fra hylden.
sentence.en: I chose a random book from the shelf.

tilfældigt.explanation: "Tilfældigt" means "randomly". It is the form of "tilfældig" (random) that describes an action. For example, "Jeg gættede tilfældigt" (I guessed randomly). To ask a polite question, use "tilfældigvis" (by chance) instead: "Har du tilfældigvis en pen?" (Do you happen to have a pen?)

sentence.da: Computeren vælger vinderen **tilfældigt** blandt alle deltagerne.
sentence.en: The computer picks the winner randomly among all the participants.

tilfældigvis.explanation: "Tilfældigvis" means "by chance". The ending "-vis" is also in "naturligvis" (of course). To ask politely for something, add it to a question: "Har du tilfældigvis en kuglepen?" (Do you happen to have a pen?).

forms.en: Do you happen to know her?

sentence.da: Jeg mødte **tilfældigvis** en gammel ven i byen.
sentence.en: I happened to meet an old friend in town.

tilgivelig.explanation: "Tilgivelig" means "forgivable". To say "unforgivable", add "u-" in front: "en utilgivelig fejl" (an unforgivable mistake).

sentence.da: Det var en **tilgivelig** fejl, fordi han var ny på arbejdet.
sentence.en: It was a forgivable mistake because he was new at work.

tilgivelse.explanation: "Tilgivelse" means "forgiveness". It comes from "at tilgive" (to forgive).

sentence.da: Han bad om **tilgivelse**, fordi han havde løjet.
sentence.en: He asked for forgiveness because he had lied.

tilgængelig.explanation: "Tilgængelig" means "available". To ask if a person has time, say: "Er du tilgængelig?" (Are you available?). To say something can be found or used, say: "Bogen er tilgængelig online" (The book is available online). It also means "accessible". For example, "Biblioteket er tilgængeligt for kørestolsbrugere" (The library is accessible for wheelchair users).

sentence.da: Informationen er **tilgængelig** for alle på nettet.
sentence.en: The information is available to everyone online.

tillid.explanation: "Tillid" means "trust". To say you trust someone, you can also use the verb "at stole på" (to rely on): "Jeg stoler på dig" (I trust you).

sentence.da: Jeg har stor **tillid** til min læge.
sentence.en: I have great trust in my doctor.

tillidsfuld.explanation: "Tillidsfuld" means "trusting". It is built from "tillid" (trust) and "-fuld" (full of).

sentence.da: Den lille dreng så **tillidsfuld** op på sin far.
sentence.en: The little boy looked up trustingly at his father.

tillykke.explanation: "Tillykke" means "congratulations". It is built from "til" (to) and "lykke" (happiness). To say what you congratulate someone on, add "med" (on): "tillykke med bilen" (congratulations on the car).

sentence.da: **Tillykke** med din nye lejlighed!
sentence.en: Congratulations on your new apartment!

tillykke med fødselsdagen.explanation: "Tillykke med fødselsdagen" means "happy birthday", literally "congratulations with the birthday".

sentence.da: Her er en gave. **Tillykke med fødselsdagen**!
sentence.en: Here is a present. Happy birthday!

tilmed.explanation: "Tilmed" means "moreover". To add one more good point, put it after "og" (and): "Maden er god, og tilmed er den billig" (The food is good, and moreover it is cheap). To say the same thing in other words, use "oven i købet" (on top of that): "Han er klog, og oven i købet er han flink" (He is smart, and on top of that he is kind).

forms.da: Det er billigt og tilmed godt
forms.en: It is cheap and also good

forms.da: Han er klog, og tilmed er han flink
forms.en: He is smart, and he is kind too

forms.da: Maden er sund og tilmed lækker
forms.en: The food is healthy and delicious too

sentence.da: Cyklen er billig, og den er **tilmed** let at reparere.
sentence.en: The bike is cheap, and it is also easy to repair.

tilpas.explanation: "Tilpas" means "just right". To say something is just right in degree, put it before an adjective: "Kaffen er tilpas stærk" (The coffee is just strong enough). To say you feel at ease, use "at føle sig" (to feel): "Jeg føler mig ikke tilpas" (I do not feel at ease).

sentence.da: Vandet er **tilpas** varmt til at bade.
sentence.en: The water is just warm enough for swimming.

tilsammen.explanation: "Tilsammen" means "in total". To add up an amount, put it after the amount: "Vi betaler 300 kroner tilsammen" (We pay 300 kroner in total). Do not mix it up with "sammen" (together), which says people do something with each other: "Vi spiser sammen" (We eat together).

forms.en: It is ten kroner in total
There are five of us in total

sentence.da: Vi er ti personer **tilsammen**.
sentence.en: We are ten people in total.

tilstedeværelse.explanation: "En tilstedeværelse" means "a presence". It is built from "til stede" (present) and "at være" (to be).

sentence.da: Lærerens **tilstedeværelse** i klassen gør børnene mere rolige.
sentence.en: The teacher's presence in the class makes the children calmer.

tilstrækkelig.explanation: "Tilstrækkelig" means "sufficient". To say something is not enough, use "at strække til" (to be enough): "Pengene strækker ikke til" (The money is not enough).

sentence.da: Fem timers søvn er ikke **tilstrækkelig** for de fleste.
sentence.en: Five hours of sleep is not sufficient for most people.

tilsyneladende.explanation: "Tilsyneladende" means "apparently". To say how things look, use it in the sentence: "Tilsyneladende er bussen forsinket" (Apparently the bus is delayed). To say you only heard it from others, use "efter sigende" (reportedly): "Han er efter sigende rig" (He is reportedly rich).

sentence.da: Butikken er **tilsyneladende** lukket i dag.
sentence.en: The store is apparently closed today.

tiltro.explanation: "En tiltro" means "a confidence". To say you trust someone, use "til" (in) after it: "Jeg har tiltro til dig" (I have confidence in you).

forms.en: to have confidence in the system

sentence.da: Efter skandalen mistede folk al **tiltro** til politikerne.
sentence.en: After the scandal, people lost all confidence in the politicians.

tiltrukket.explanation: "Tiltrukket" means "attracted". It comes from "at tiltrække" (to attract). To name the person or thing that attracts you, use "af" (by): "Hun er tiltrukket af ham" (She is attracted to him).

forms.en: We are drawn to the city

sentence.da: Bierne er **tiltrukket** af blomsternes søde duft.
sentence.en: The bees are attracted to the sweet scent of the flowers.

tiltrækkende.explanation: "Tiltrækkende" means "attractive". It comes from "at tiltrække" (to attract). Do not mix it up with "tiltrukket" (attracted), which is about the one who feels pulled. For example, "Han er tiltrukket af hende, for hun er tiltrækkende" (He is attracted to her, because she is attractive).

sentence.da: Prisen gør tilbuddet meget **tiltrækkende**.
sentence.en: The price makes the offer very attractive.

timevis.explanation: "Timevis" means "for hours". It is built from "en time" (an hour) and the ending "-vis". The same ending makes "dagevis" (for days).

sentence.da: Jeg kan sidde **timevis** med en god bog.
sentence.en: I can sit for hours with a good book.

tirsdag.explanation: "Tirsdag" means "Tuesday". In Danish, day names are not capitalized, unlike English "Tuesday". To say "on Tuesday" for the coming one, use "på tirsdag": "Vi ses på tirsdag" (See you on Tuesday). To say you do something every Tuesday, use "om tirsdagen": "Jeg træner om tirsdagen" (I work out on Tuesdays).

sentence.da: Efter mandag kommer **tirsdag**.
sentence.en: After Monday comes Tuesday.

tja.explanation: "Tja" means "well". Use it when you are unsure and still thinking: "Kommer du?" "Tja, måske." (Are you coming? Well, maybe.)

sentence.da: **Tja**, jeg ved ikke helt, hvad jeg skal sige.
sentence.en: Well, I do not quite know what to say.

to.explanation: "To" means "two". To count things, put it before the noun: "to børn" (two children), "to æg" (two eggs). In numbers like 22 the ones come first. For example, "toogtyve" (twenty-two) is literally "two-and-twenty".

sentence.da: En, **to**, tre!
sentence.en: One, two, three!

to gange.explanation: "To gange" means "twice". Literally, it is "two times". To say how often something happens, add "om dagen" (a day), "om ugen" (a week) or "om måneden" (a month): "to gange om ugen" (twice a week).

sentence.da: Én gang, **to gange**, tre gange!
sentence.en: Once, twice, three times!

tofu.explanation: "Tofu" means "tofu". To name an amount, say "en pakke tofu" (a package of tofu).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have **tofu** i stedet for kød.
sentence.en: I would like tofu instead of meat.

toiletpapir.explanation: "Toiletpapir" means "toilet paper". It is built from "et toilet" (a toilet) and "papir" (paper). To name an amount, say "en rulle toiletpapir" (a roll of toilet paper).

sentence.da: Man bruger **toiletpapir** på toilettet.
sentence.en: You use toilet paper in the bathroom.

told.explanation: "Told" means "customs". It also means a tax on goods from abroad, which English calls "duty". For example, "Man skal betale told" (You have to pay duty).

sentence.da: Der er lang kø ved **told** i lufthavnen.
sentence.en: There is a long line at customs at the airport.

tolerant.explanation: "Tolerant" means "tolerant", spelled the same as in English. To say the opposite, add "in-": "en intolerant person" (an intolerant person).

sentence.da: Et **tolerant** samfund giver plads til alle slags mennesker.
sentence.en: A tolerant society makes room for all kinds of people.

tolv.explanation: "Tolv" means "twelve". To say a dozen, use "et dusin": "et dusin æg" (a dozen eggs).

sentence.da: Efter elleve kommer **tolv**.
sentence.en: After eleven comes twelve.

tolvte.explanation: "Tolvte" means "twelfth". To say a date, use "den tolvte december" (the twelfth of December).

sentence.da: Dagen efter den elvte er den **tolvte**.
sentence.en: The day after the eleventh is the twelfth.

tom.explanation: "Tom" means "empty". To say the opposite, use "fuld" (full): "en fuld flaske" (a full bottle). The word "fuld" also means "drunk" for a person. For example, "Han er fuld" (He is drunk).

sentence.da: Der er intet vand. Flasken er **tom**.
sentence.en: There is no water. The bottle is empty.

tomhændet.explanation: "Tomhændet" means "empty-handed". It is built from "tom" (empty) and "en hånd" (a hand).

sentence.da: Hun købte blomster, fordi hun ikke ville komme **tomhændet**.
sentence.en: She bought flowers because she did not want to come empty-handed.

torden.explanation: "Torden" means "thunder". It is the noun for "at tordne" (to thunder). To say it is thundering right now, say "Det tordner" (It is thundering).

sentence.da: Efter lyn kommer **torden**.
sentence.en: After lightning comes thunder.

torsdag.explanation: "Torsdag" means "Thursday". In Danish, day names are not capitalized, unlike English "Thursday". To say "on Thursday" for the coming one, use "på torsdag": "Vi ses på torsdag" (See you on Thursday). To say "on Thursdays", use "om torsdagen": "Jeg træner om torsdagen" (I work out on Thursdays). Do not mix it up with "tirsdag" (Tuesday). For example, "Vi ses torsdag" (See you Thursday), "Vi ses tirsdag" (See you Tuesday).

sentence.da: Efter onsdag kommer **torsdag**.
sentence.en: After Wednesday comes Thursday.

torsk.explanation: "Torsk" means "cod". To talk about the animal, say "en torsk" (a cod). To talk about the food, use "torsk" alone: "Vi spiser torsk" (We eat cod).

sentence.da: Fiskeren fanger en stor **torsk** i havet.
sentence.en: The fisherman catches a big cod in the sea.

tortur.explanation: "En tortur" means "torture". It also describes something very unpleasant. For example, "Det var en tortur at vente" (Waiting was torture).

sentence.da: **Tortur** er at gøre ondt på et menneske med vilje.
sentence.en: Torture is hurting a person on purpose.

tosproget.explanation: "Tosproget" means "bilingual". It is built from "to" (two) and "et sprog" (a language). It also describes things in two languages. For example, "et tosproget skilt" (a bilingual sign).

sentence.da: Hun er **tosproget** og taler både dansk og engelsk hjemme.
sentence.en: She is bilingual and speaks both Danish and English at home.

tosset.explanation: "Tosset" means "silly". A silly person is called "en tosse" (a silly person).

sentence.da: Han er **tosset**, men ikke farlig.
sentence.en: He is silly, but not dangerous.

total.explanation: "Total" means "total". To make another word stronger, use "totalt" (totally) before it: "Jeg er totalt træt" (I am totally tired).

sentence.da: Det var en **total** katastrofe, og alle var kede af det.
sentence.en: It was a total disaster, and everyone was upset about it.

totalt.explanation: "Totalt" means "totally". It is built from "total" (total) and the ending "-t". To make an adjective stronger, put it before: "Han er totalt ligeglad" (He does not care at all).

sentence.da: Jeg er **totalt** træt efter turen.
sentence.en: I am totally tired after the trip.

traditionel.explanation: "Traditionel" means "traditional". To say traditional food, use "traditionel mad" (traditional food). To say the opposite, use "moderne" (modern): "et moderne hus" (a modern house).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **traditionel** mad til jul.
sentence.en: We eat traditional food at Christmas.

trafik.explanation: "Trafik" means "traffic". To say a traffic jam, use "en trafikprop" (literally, a traffic plug): "Der er en trafikprop på broen" (There is a traffic jam on the bridge).

sentence.da: Der er meget **trafik** på motorvejen i dag.
sentence.en: There is a lot of traffic on the highway today.

tragisk.explanation: "Tragisk" means "tragic". The noun is "en tragedie" (a tragedy). For example, "Branden var en tragedie" (The fire was a tragedy).

sentence.da: Det var en **tragisk** dag, og alle græd.
sentence.en: It was a tragic day, and everyone cried.

trang.explanation: "Trang" means "cramped". To say a room has too little space, use it before the noun: "et trangt rum" (a cramped room). For clothes it means "tight": "trange bukser" (tight pants). To talk about little money, use "trange kår" (hard circumstances): "at leve på trange kår" (to live on very little).

sentence.da: I en **trang** lejlighed er der næsten ikke plads til møbler.
sentence.en: In a cramped apartment there is hardly room for furniture.

travl.explanation: "Travl" means "busy". To say you are in a hurry, use "at have det travlt" (to be in a hurry): "Jeg har det travlt" (I am in a hurry).

sentence.da: Jeg har meget at lave. Jeg er **travl**.
sentence.en: I have a lot to do. I am busy.

tre.explanation: "Tre" means "three". To count things, put it before the noun: "tre børn" (three children), "tre æg" (three eggs).

sentence.da: Efter to kommer **tre**.
sentence.en: After two comes three.

tredive.explanation: "Tredive" means "thirty". To say 31, put the one first: "enogtredive" (thirty-one), literally "one-and-thirty".

sentence.da: Tyve, **tredive**, fyrre.
sentence.en: Twenty, thirty, forty.

tredje.explanation: "Tredje" means "third". To give a date, say: "den tredje oktober" (the third of October).

sentence.da: Den første, den anden og den **tredje**.
sentence.en: The first, the second and the third.

tres.explanation: "Tres" means "sixty". Do not mix it up with "tre" (three). For example, "tre børn" means three children, and "tres børn" means sixty children.

sentence.da: Halvtreds, **tres**, halvfjerds.
sentence.en: Fifty, sixty, seventy.

tretten.explanation: "Tretten" means "thirteen". To say how many things there are, put it before the noun: "tretten æg" (thirteen eggs).

sentence.da: Tolv, **tretten**, fjorten.
sentence.en: Twelve, thirteen, fourteen.

trist.explanation: "Trist" means "sad". Besides a person who feels sad, it also describes a gloomy thing. To describe gray weather, say: "Vejret er trist i dag" (The weather is gloomy today).

sentence.da: Hun er **trist** og græder.
sentence.en: She is sad and crying.

trivsel.explanation: "Trivsel" means "well-being". It comes from the verb "at trives" (to thrive). To say you feel at home somewhere, use the verb: "Jeg trives her" (I feel at home here).

sentence.da: Skolen arbejder for børnenes **trivsel**, så ingen skal føle sig alene.
sentence.en: The school works for the children's well-being, so that no one feels alone.

tro.explanation: "Tro" means "faith". To say someone keeps their faith, say: "Hun mister aldrig sin tro" (She never loses her faith). To say you think something is true, use the verb "at tro" (to believe): "Jeg tror, det er rigtigt" (I think it is right).

sentence.da: Hendes **tro** på Gud giver hende ro.
sentence.en: Her faith in God gives her peace.

trods.explanation: "Trods" means "despite". To say what you went on despite, name the obstacle right after it: "trods regnen" (despite the rain).

sentence.da: **Trods** den høje pris købte hun den dyre jakke.
sentence.en: Despite the high price, she bought the expensive jacket.

trods alt.explanation: "Trods alt" means "after all". It is built from "trods" (despite) and "alt" (everything), so it is literally "despite everything". To say the evening was good in the end: "Var festen god?" "Ja, det var trods alt en god aften." (Was the party good? Yes, it was a good evening after all.)

forms.en: She got the job after all.

sentence.da: Der var mange problemer, men vi nåede **trods alt** frem.
sentence.en: There were many problems, but we got there after all.

troende.explanation: "Troende" means "believing". It comes from the verb "at tro" (to believe). To describe a person who has a faith, say: "en troende muslim" (a believing Muslim). With "de" (the), it names the people. For example, "de troende" (the believers).

sentence.da: Hun er en **troende** kvinde og går i kirke hver søndag.
sentence.en: She is a religious woman and goes to church every Sunday.

trofast.explanation: "Trofast" means "faithful". It is built from "tro" (loyal) and "fast" (firm). To say a partner cheated, use the opposite, "utro" (unfaithful): "Han var utro" (He was unfaithful).

sentence.da: Min hund er en **trofast** ven, som venter ved døren.
sentence.en: My dog is a faithful friend who waits at the door.

troskab.explanation: "Troskab" means "loyalty". It is built from "tro" (faithful) and "-skab", an ending that makes a noun, as in "venskab" (friendship). To name the opposite, say: "Utroskab ødelagde ægteskabet" (Infidelity ruined the marriage).

sentence.da: Soldaten svor **troskab** mod kongen.
sentence.en: The soldier swore loyalty to the king.

trusser.explanation: "Trusser" means "panties". It is plural, like "panties" in English. For men's underwear, say "underbukser" (underpants): "Jeg har købt nye underbukser" (I bought new underpants).

sentence.da: Hun tager **trusser** og bukser på.
sentence.en: She puts on panties and pants.

tryg.explanation: "Tryg" means "safe", as in feeling looked after. To say children feel safe with someone: "Børnene er trygge hos deres bedstemor" (The children feel safe with their grandmother). To say you feel uneasy, use the opposite, "utryg" (uneasy): "Han er utryg ved at flyve" (He is uneasy about flying).

sentence.da: Jeg føler mig **tryg** sammen med dig.
sentence.en: I feel safe with you.

tryghed.explanation: "Tryghed" means "security". It is built from the adjective "tryg" (safe) and the ending "-hed". To say something gives security, use it with "at give" (to give): "Rutiner giver børn tryghed" (Routines give children security).

sentence.da: Børn har brug for **tryghed** hjemme.
sentence.en: Children need security at home.

trygt.explanation: "Trygt" means "safely". It comes from the adjective "tryg" (safe). To tell someone they need not worry about doing something, say: "Du kan trygt spørge" (You can safely ask).

forms.en: You can move about safely here

sentence.da: Børn skal kunne lege **trygt** i deres eget kvarter.
sentence.en: Children should be able to play safely in their own neighborhood.

trådløs.explanation: "Trådløs" means "wireless". It is built from "tråd" (wire) and "-løs" (-less).

sentence.da: Min nye højttaler er **trådløs** og har ikke noget kabel.
sentence.en: My new speaker is wireless and has no cable.

træg.explanation: "Træg" means "sluggish". To say you have little energy, say: "Jeg føler mig træg i dag" (I feel sluggish today).

sentence.da: Trafikken var **træg**, fordi der var mange biler.
sentence.en: The traffic was sluggish because there were many cars.

træning.explanation: "Træning" means "training session". It comes from the verb "at træne" (to train). To say you have practice, use it with "at have" (to have): "Jeg har træning i aften" (I have training tonight).

sentence.da: Efter **træning** er jeg altid sulten og træt.
sentence.en: After training I am always hungry and tired.

træningstøj.explanation: "Træningstøj" means "workout clothes". It is built from "træning" (training) and "tøj" (clothes). To remind someone to pack it for the gym: "Husk dit træningstøj" (Remember your workout clothes).

sentence.da: Jeg har **træningstøj** på, når jeg løber.
sentence.en: I wear workout clothes when I run.

træt.explanation: "Træt" means "tired". To say you are fed up with something, add "af" (of): "Jeg er træt af støjen" (I am fed up with the noise).

sentence.da: Jeg er meget **træt** og vil sove.
sentence.en: I am very tired and want to sleep.

træt af.explanation: "Træt af" means "tired of". To say you have had enough of something: "Jeg er træt af støjen" (I am tired of the noise). Without "af", it is about needing sleep. For example, "Jeg er træt" (I am tired).

sentence.da: Jeg er **træt af** at vente her.
sentence.en: I am tired of waiting here.

træthed.explanation: "Træthed" means "tiredness". It is built from the adjective "træt" (tired) and the ending "-hed". To say you are struggling with it: "Jeg kæmper med træthed" (I am struggling with tiredness).

sentence.da: Manglende søvn giver **træthed** og dårlig koncentration.
sentence.en: Lack of sleep causes tiredness and poor concentration.

trøst.explanation: "Trøst" means "comfort", as in consolation for someone who is sad. To say something helps only a little, say: "Det er en lille trøst" (That is a small comfort).

sentence.da: Hun fandt **trøst** hos sine venner.
sentence.en: She found comfort with her friends.

tun.explanation: "Tun" means "tuna". It joins other words, as in "tunsalat" (tuna salad). For example, "Jeg tager en sandwich med tunsalat" (I will take a sandwich with tuna salad).

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser jeg **tun** med salat.
sentence.en: For lunch I eat tuna with salad.

tung.explanation: "Tung" means "heavy". To say food feels heavy in the stomach, say: "tung mad" (heavy food).

sentence.da: Tasken er meget **tung** at løfte.
sentence.en: The bag is very heavy to lift.

turkis.explanation: "Turkis" means "turquoise". English speakers should spell it with a "k" where English has "qu".

sentence.da: Blå og grøn bliver **turkis**.
sentence.en: Blue and green make turquoise.

tusind.explanation: "Tusind" means "thousand". To say a year, count in hundreds instead: 1999 is "nitten hundrede og nioghalvfems" (nineteen hundred and ninety-nine).

sentence.da: Ti gange hundrede er **tusind**.
sentence.en: Ten times a hundred is a thousand.

tusind tak.explanation: "Tusind tak" means "thanks a lot", literally "a thousand thanks". To thank a host after a meal, add "for" and what you thank for: "Tusind tak for maden" (Thanks a lot for the meal).

forms.en: Thanks a lot for your help.

forms.da: Tusind tak, det var pænt af dig.
forms.en: Thanks a lot, that was kind of you.

sentence.da: Du har hjulpet mig så meget. **Tusind tak**!
sentence.en: You have helped me so much. Thanks a lot!

tusindvis.explanation: "Tusindvis" means "thousands". To say what is counted, add "af" (of) and the noun: "tusindvis af mennesker" (thousands of people).

sentence.da: Ved en stor koncert er der **tusindvis** af mennesker.
sentence.en: At a big concert there are thousands of people.

tvetydig.explanation: "Tvetydig" means "ambiguous". The start "tve-" means "two", as in "tvilling" (twin).

sentence.da: Det er en **tvetydig** sætning, for den kan forstås på to måder.
sentence.en: It is an ambiguous sentence, because it can be understood in two ways.

tvivlsom.explanation: "Tvivlsom" means "doubtful". It is built from "tvivl" (doubt) and the ending "-som". To say a person feels unsure, use "usikker" (unsure): "Jeg er usikker" (I am unsure).

sentence.da: Jeg synes, hans forklaring er meget **tvivlsom**.
sentence.en: I think his explanation is very doubtful.

tvungen.explanation: "Tvungen" means "forced". It comes from the verb "at tvinge" (to force). To say who is forced to do what, use "til at" (into): "De tvinger ham til at flytte" (They are forcing him to move).

sentence.da: Det var ikke et frit valg, men en **tvungen** løsning.
sentence.en: It was not a free choice but a forced solution.

tværtimod.explanation: "Tværtimod" means "on the contrary". To answer a question by saying the opposite is true: "Generer jeg dig?" "Tværtimod!" (Am I bothering you? On the contrary!)

forms.en: It is not expensive, on the contrary.
On the contrary, it was a pleasure.

sentence.da: Han er ikke doven, **tværtimod** arbejder han meget.
sentence.en: He is not lazy; on the contrary, he works a lot.

tydelig.explanation: "Tydelig" means "clear", as in easy to see or understand. To ask someone to speak so you can understand, say: "Tal tydeligt" (Speak clearly). For clear water or clear skies, use "klar" (clear): "klart vand" (clear water).

sentence.da: Hendes stemme er **tydelig**, så alle kan høre hende.
sentence.en: Her voice is clear, so everyone can hear her.

tydeligvis.explanation: "Tydeligvis" means "obviously". It is built from "tydelig" (clear) and "-vis", an ending like English "-ly". To say the signs show nobody is home: "Der er tydeligvis ingen hjemme" (Obviously nobody is home).

sentence.da: Han er **tydeligvis** hjemme, fordi der er lys i vinduet.
sentence.en: He is obviously home because there is a light in the window.

tyggegummi.explanation: "Tyggegummi" means "chewing gum". It is built from "at tygge" (to chew) and "gummi" (rubber). The part "gummi" also appears in "gummistøvler" (rubber boots).

sentence.da: Børnene tygger **tyggegummi** og blæser store bobler.
sentence.en: The kids chew chewing gum and blow big bubbles.

tyk.explanation: "Tyk" means "thick". To say a jacket is thick: "Jakken er tyk" (The jacket is thick). About a person it means "fat" and is as blunt as that English word.

sentence.da: Bogen har mange sider. Den er **tyk**.
sentence.en: The book has many pages. It is thick.

tynd.explanation: "Tynd" means "thin". It also describes watery liquids. For example, "tynd suppe" (thin soup). To describe a person as slim, say "slank" (slim): "Hun er slank" (She is slim).

sentence.da: Bogen har få sider. Den er **tynd**.
sentence.en: The book has few pages. It is thin.

tyngdekraft.explanation: "Tyngdekraft" means "gravity". It is built from "tyngde" (weight) and "kraft" (force), so it is literally "weight force". To say why things fall: "Tyngdekraften trækker tingene ned" (Gravity pulls things down).

sentence.da: Uden **tyngdekraft** ville tingene svæve rundt i luften.
sentence.en: Without gravity things would float around in the air.

typisk.explanation: "Typisk" means "typical". To complain that something bad happened again, say just: "Typisk!" (Typical!)

sentence.da: Det er en **typisk** dansk ret med kartofler.
sentence.en: It is a typical Danish dish with potatoes.

tyrkiet.explanation: "Tyrkiet" means "Turkey", as in the country. To say the bird, use "en kalkun" (a turkey): "Jeg har en kalkun i ovnen" (I have a turkey in the oven).

sentence.da: Istanbul er en stor by i **Tyrkiet**.
sentence.en: Istanbul is a big city in Turkey.

tyrkisk.explanation: "Tyrkisk" means "Turkish". To ask whether someone knows the language: "Kan du tyrkisk?" (Do you know Turkish?)

sentence.da: Hun kommer fra Tyrkiet og taler **tyrkisk**.
sentence.en: She comes from Turkey and speaks Turkish.

tysk.explanation: "Tysk" means "German". To name the school subject: "Vi har tysk i dag" (We have German today).

sentence.da: Han kommer fra Tyskland og taler **tysk**.
sentence.en: He comes from Germany and speaks German.

tyskland.explanation: "Tyskland" means "Germany". It is built from "tysk" (German) and "land" (country). Germany is the only country that shares a land border with Denmark.

sentence.da: Berlin er en stor by i **Tyskland**.
sentence.en: Berlin is a big city in Germany.

tyve.explanation: "Tyve" means "twenty". To say 22, put the two first: "toogtyve" (twenty-two), literally "two-and-twenty".

sentence.da: Ti og ti er **tyve**.
sentence.en: Ten and ten is twenty.

tyvende.explanation: "Tyvende" means "twentieth". To name the 1900s, say: "det tyvende århundrede" (the twentieth century).

sentence.da: Efter den nittende dag kommer den **tyvende**.
sentence.en: After the nineteenth day comes the twentieth.

tåbelig.explanation: "Tåbelig" means "foolish". To say "stupid" in everyday speech, use "dum": "Det var en dum idé" (That was a stupid idea).

sentence.da: Det var en **tåbelig** idé at gå ud uden jakke.
sentence.en: It was a foolish idea to go out without a jacket.

tåge.explanation: "Tåge" means "fog". To say the weather is foggy, use the adjective "tåget" (foggy): "Det er tåget i dag" (It is foggy today).

sentence.da: Man kan ikke se langt i **tåge**.
sentence.en: You cannot see far in fog.

tålmodig.explanation: "Tålmodig" means "patient". The opposite is "utålmodig" (impatient). For example, "Børnene er utålmodige" (The children are impatient).

related.en: to bear, to put up with

sentence.da: Hun er **tålmodig** og venter uden at klage.
sentence.en: She is patient and waits without complaining.

tålmodighed.explanation: "Tålmodighed" means "patience". It is built from the adjective "tålmodig" (patient) and the ending "-hed". To tell someone to be patient: "Vær tålmodig" (Be patient).

sentence.da: Det kræver **tålmodighed** at lære et nyt sprog.
sentence.en: It takes patience to learn a new language.

tæt.explanation: "Tæt" means "dense". To describe thick fog: "Der er tæt tåge" (There is dense fog). To say a place is close, use "tæt på" (close to): "Jeg bor tæt på skolen" (I live close to the school).

sentence.da: Taget er **tæt**, og regnen kommer ikke ind.
sentence.en: The roof is watertight, and the rain does not come in.

tæt på.explanation: "Tæt på" means "close to". To say you nearly did something: "Han var tæt på at vinde" (He came close to winning). To say a place is far away, use "langt fra" (far from): "Skolen ligger langt fra stationen" (The school is far from the station).

sentence.da: Hotellet ligger **tæt på** stranden.
sentence.en: The hotel is close to the beach.

tøj.explanation: "Tøj" means "clothes". This word has no article, so leave out "et": say "mit tøj" (my clothes) or "noget tøj" (some clothes). To point to one piece of clothing, use its name: "en trøje" (a sweater).

sentence.da: Bukser og trøjer er **tøj**.
sentence.en: Pants and sweaters are clothes.

tømmer.explanation: "Tømmer" means "timber". Do not mix it up with "tømmer" from "at tømme" (to empty). For example, "Jeg tømmer skabet" (I empty the cabinet).

sentence.da: Vi bruger **tømmer** fra skoven til at bygge huset.
sentence.en: We use timber from the forest to build the house.

tømmermænd.explanation: "Tømmermænd" means "a hangover". The word is always plural. To say you have one: "Jeg har tømmermænd" (I have a hangover).

sentence.da: Efter festen havde han **tømmermænd** og ville bare sove.
sentence.en: After the party he had a hangover and just wanted to sleep.

tør.explanation: "Tør" means "dry". It is also a form of the verb "at turde" (to dare). For example, "Jeg tør ikke" (I dare not).

sentence.da: Jakken var våd. Nu er den **tør**.
sentence.en: The jacket was wet. Now it is dry.

tørret frugt.explanation: "Tørret frugt" means "dried fruit". "Tørret" (dried) comes from the verb "at tørre" (to dry). To say what you add to your porridge: "Jeg putter tørret frugt i havregrøden" (I put dried fruit in the porridge).

sentence.da: Rosiner og abrikoser er **tørret frugt**.
sentence.en: Raisins and apricots are dried fruit.

tørstig.explanation: "Tørstig" means "thirsty". The noun is "tørst" (thirst). To say you are thirsty, use it with "at have" (to have): "Jeg har tørst" (I am thirsty), literally "I have thirst".

sentence.da: Jeg er **tørstig** og vil have vand.
sentence.en: I am thirsty and want water.
